title.zh: 卷四十八 列傳第四十二 儒林
title.raw: 卷四十八 列傳第四十二 儒林 Volume 48: Confucian Scholars

sentences.zh: 漢氏承秦燔書，大弘儒訓，太學生徒，動以萬數，郡國黌舍，悉皆充滿。

translations.literal: The Han, inheriting Qin's burning of books, greatly expanded Confucian instruction; Imperial University students often numbered in the tens of thousands, and district and commandery schoolhouses were all filled.
translations.idiomatic: Han, after Qin's book-burning, greatly promoted Confucian learning—Imperial University enrollees often ran to tens of thousands, and every district school was full.

sentences.zh: 學於山澤者，至或就爲列肆，其盛也如是。

translations.literal: Those studying in mountains and marshes might even set up as shop rows—the flourishing was such.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars in remote hills sometimes opened roadside stalls to teach—the scale was that great.

sentences.zh: 漢末喪亂，其道遂衰。

translations.literal: At the end of Han, amid turmoil and ruin, the Way declined.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han chaos made the tradition fade.

sentences.zh: 魏正始以後，仍尚玄虛之學，爲儒者蓋寡。

translations.literal: After Wei's Zhengshi era, dark and empty learning was still honored, and Confucians were few.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei's Zhengshi reign on, abstruse learning held sway and few remained true Confucians.

sentences.zh: 時荀顗、摯虞之徒，雖刪定新禮，改官職，未能易俗移風。

translations.literal: At the time Xun Yi, Zhi Yu, and their like, though they revised the new rites and changed offices and ranks, could not alter custom or shift the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi, Zhi Yu, and others revised rites and offices but could not change society.

sentences.zh: 自是中原橫潰，衣冠殄盡；

translations.literal: From then on the Central Plains collapsed in ruin, and the gentry were wiped out;
translations.idiomatic: Then the heartland collapsed and the elite perished;

sentences.zh: 江左草創，日不暇給；

translations.literal: the left bank of the Yangtze was newly founded, with not a day to spare;
translations.idiomatic: the south was newly settled, with no leisure for anything else;

sentences.zh: 以迄于宋、齊。

translations.literal: and so it continued through Song and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: and so it went through Song and Qi.

sentences.zh: 國學時或開置，而勸課未博，建之不及十年，蓋取文具，廢之多歷世祀，其棄也忽諸。

translations.literal: The National University was sometimes opened, yet encouragement of study was not broad; establishments rarely lasted ten years—mostly for show on paper—while abandonment stretched over many generations; it was cast aside as if trivial.
translations.idiomatic: The National University opened now and then, but study was not widely urged; it rarely stood ten years, was often mere form, and was neglected for generations.

sentences.zh: 鄉里莫或開館，公卿罕通經術。

translations.literal: In the villages none opened halls; among ministers and grandees few mastered the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Villages had no schools; high officials rarely knew the classics.

sentences.zh: 朝廷大儒，獨學而弗肯養衆；

translations.literal: Great scholars at court studied alone and would not nurture the multitude;
translations.idiomatic: Court masters studied alone and would not teach crowds;

sentences.zh: 後生孤陋，擁經而無所講習。

translations.literal: the young were isolated and narrow, clutching the classics with no one to lecture and practice with.
translations.idiomatic: youth were isolated, holding texts with no one to instruct them.

sentences.zh: 三德六藝，其廢久矣。

translations.literal: The three virtues and six arts had long been abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The three virtues and six arts had long lain in ruin.

sentences.zh: 高祖有天下，深愍之，詔求碩學，治五禮，定六律，改鬥曆，正權衡。

translations.literal: When Gaozu gained the realm he deeply lamented this and issued an edict seeking eminent scholars to regulate the five rites, fix the six pitch-pipes, revise the dipper calendar, and correct weights and measures.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, having won the realm, deeply regretted this and ordered a search for great scholars to settle the five rites, six pitch-pipes, calendar, and weights.

sentences.zh: 天監四年，詔曰：「二漢登賢，莫非經術，服膺雅道，名立行成。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianjian an edict said: "In the two Han dynasties those who rose to office were all through classical learning; embracing the elegant Way, they established names and completed conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year four an edict said: "Under the two Han, promotion came through the classics; embracing the Way, men won fame and formed character.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉浮蕩，儒教淪歇，風節罔樹，抑此之由。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin drifted in frivolity, Confucian teaching sank and ceased, and standards of conduct were not planted—this is the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin grew frivolous, Confucian teaching collapsed, and morals were not built—that is why.

sentences.zh: 朕日昃罷朝，思聞俊異，收士得人，實惟酬獎。

translations.literal: I, from morning to evening after court, think to hear of outstanding men; to gather scholars and gain men is truly a matter of reward.
translations.idiomatic: I, weary from dawn court, long to hear of talent; to gather scholars deserves reward.

sentences.zh: 可置《五經》博士各一人，廣開館宇，招內後進。

translations.literal: Let there be one Erudite for each of the Five Classics, broadly open halls, and recruit the young within.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint one Erudite per Five Classic, open halls widely, and recruit young students.

sentences.zh: 」於是以平原明山賓、吳興沈峻、建平嚴植之、會稽賀瑒補博士，各主一館。

translations.literal: "; Thereupon Ming Shanbin of Pingyuan, Shen Jun of Wuxing, Yan Zhizhi of Jianping, and He Chang of Kuaiji were appointed erudites, each presiding over one hall.
translations.idiomatic: "; then Ming Shanbin of Pingyuan, Shen Jun of Wuxing, Yan Zhizhi of Jianping, and He Chang of Kuaiji became erudites, each heading a hall.

sentences.zh: 館有數百生，給其餼廩。

translations.literal: Each hall had several hundred students, supplied with grain stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Each hall held hundreds of students on grain stipends.

sentences.zh: 其射策通明者，卽除爲吏。

translations.literal: Those who in the archery examination showed penetrating mastery were at once appointed officials.
translations.idiomatic: Those who passed the archery examination with clear mastery were made officials at once.

sentences.zh: 十數月間，懷經負笈者雲會京師。

translations.literal: Within a dozen months those bearing the classics in satchels on their backs gathered at the capital like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Within months scholars with satchels of classics flocked to the capital.

sentences.zh: 又選遣學生如會稽雲門山，受業於廬江何胤。

translations.literal: Students were also selected and sent to Cloud Gate Mountain in Kuaiji to study under He Yin of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Students were sent to Cloud Gate Mountain in Kuaiji to study with He Yin of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 分遣博士祭酒，到州郡立學。

translations.literal: Erudites and libationers were dispatched to establish schools in prefectures and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites and libationers were sent to found schools in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 七年，又詔曰：「建國君民，立教爲首，砥身礪行，由乎經術。

translations.literal: In the seventh year another edict said: "To found a state and rule the people, establishing teaching comes first; to polish the person and sharpen conduct depends on classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven another edict said: "To found a state and govern the people, teaching comes first; self-cultivation depends on the classics.

sentences.zh: 朕肇基明命，光宅區宇，雖耕耘雅業，傍闡藝文，而成器未廣，志本猶闕。

translations.literal: I, at the beginning of bright mandate, have made the realm my dwelling; though I have cultivated elegant pursuits and opened arts on every side, finished vessels are not yet broad and the root of intent is still lacking.
translations.idiomatic: I began with bright mandate and hold the realm; though I have pursued learning and arts, too few are fully formed and the root of intent still lacks.

sentences.zh: 非以鎔範貴游，納諸軌度；

translations.literal: It is not to mold and cast the noble scions and bring them within measure;
translations.idiomatic: It is not merely to mold noble youth into measure;

sentences.zh: 思欲式敦讓齒，自家刑國。

translations.literal: I wish to model deep respect for elders and, from the family, impose law on the state.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to honor elders and let family discipline shape the state.

sentences.zh: 今聲訓所漸，戎夏同風。

translations.literal: Now where sound and instruction reach, barbarian and Chinese share one wind.
translations.idiomatic: Now where teaching reaches, barbarians and Chinese share one custom.

sentences.zh: 宜大啓痒斅，博延胄子，務彼十倫，弘此三德，使陶鈞遠被，微言載表。

translations.literal: Let the great schools be broadly opened, the sons of the nobility widely gathered, attend to those ten bonds, and spread these three virtues, so that the potter's wheel reaches far and subtle words are set forth.
translations.idiomatic: Open the great schools, gather noble sons, uphold the ten bonds and three virtues, so teaching reaches far and subtle doctrine is displayed.

sentences.zh: 」於是皇太子、皇子、宗室、王侯始就業焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the crown prince, princes, imperial clansmen, kings, and marquises first took up study.
translations.idiomatic: Then crown prince, princes, imperial kin, kings, and marquises began their studies.

sentences.zh: 高祖親屈輿駕，釋奠於先師先聖，申之以讌語，勞之以束帛，濟濟焉，洋洋焉，大道之行也如是。

translations.literal: Gaozu himself bent the carriage and performed the offering sacrifice to the former teacher and former sage, followed it with feasting talk, and rewarded them with silks—vast and grand was the procession of the Great Way.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu himself came in his carriage to sacrifice to the ancient sages, feasted and spoke with them, and gave silk gifts—so grandly did the Great Way proceed.

sentences.zh: 其伏曼容、何佟之、范縝，有舊名於世；

translations.literal: Fu Manrong, He Tongzhi, and Fan Zhen had old fame in the world;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Manrong, He Tongzhi, and Fan Zhen were already famed;

sentences.zh: 爲時儒者，嚴植之、賀瑒等首膺茲選。

translations.literal: among contemporary Confucians, Yan Zhizhi, He Chang, and others were first chosen for these posts.
translations.idiomatic: among scholars of the day Yan Zhizhi, He Chang, and others led the appointments.

sentences.zh: 今並綴爲《儒林傳》云。

translations.literal: Now they are all gathered into this "Biographies of Confucian Scholars."
translations.idiomatic: They are now collected in this Biography of Confucian Scholars.

sentences.zh: 伏曼容

translations.literal: Fu Manrong
translations.idiomatic: Fu Manrong

sentences.zh: 伏曼容字公儀，平昌安丘人。

translations.literal: Fu Manrong, courtesy name Gongyi, was a man of Anqiu in Pingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Manrong, styled Gongyi, was from Anqiu in Pingchang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖滔，晉著作郎。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Tao was Jin Director of Composition.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Tao was Jin Director of Composition.

sentences.zh: 父胤之，宋司空主簿。

translations.literal: His father Yin-zhi was Song Master of Records in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yin-zhi was Song Master of Records in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 曼容早孤，與母兄客居南海。

translations.literal: Manrong lost his father early and lived as a guest in Nanhai with his mother and elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Manrong was orphaned young and lodged in Nanhai with his mother and brother.

sentences.zh: 少篤學，善《老》、《易》，倜儻好大言，常云：「何晏疑《易》中九事。

translations.literal: In youth he was devoted to learning, skilled in the Laozi and Changes, bold and fond of grand talk, and often said: "He Yan doubted nine matters in the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Young, he studied hard, knew the Laozi and Changes, was bold and fond of bold talk, and often said: "He Yan doubted nine points in the Changes.

sentences.zh: 以吾觀之，晏了不學也，故知平叔有所短。

translations.literal: In my view Yan did not study at all—thus one knows Ping-shu had his shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: By my lights Yan never studied—so Ping-shu had his flaws.

sentences.zh: 」聚徒教授以自業。

translations.literal: " He gathered pupils and taught to make his living.
translations.idiomatic: "; he gathered students and taught for a living.

sentences.zh: 爲驃騎行參軍。

translations.literal: He served as staff aide to the Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: He was staff aide to the Rapid Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝好《周易》，集朝臣於清暑殿講，詔曼容執經。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song loved the Book of Changes, gathered court ministers in the Clear Summer Hall to lecture, and ordered Manrong to hold the classic.
translations.idiomatic: Song Emperor Ming loved the Changes, gathered the court in Clear Summer Hall, and had Manrong hold the text.

sentences.zh: 曼容素美風采，帝恒以方嵇叔夜，使吳人陸探微畫叔夜像以賜之。

translations.literal: Manrong was always handsome in bearing; the emperor constantly compared him to Ji Kang and had the Wu man Lu Tanwei paint Ji Kang's portrait to give him.
translations.idiomatic: Manrong was handsome; the emperor likened him to Ji Kang and had Lu Tanwei paint Ji Kang's image as a gift.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒參軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Secretariat staff aide.
translations.idiomatic: He became Secretariat staff aide.

sentences.zh: 袁粲爲丹陽尹，請爲江寧令，入拜尚書外兵郎。

translations.literal: When Yuan Can was Governor of Danyang he invited him as magistrate of Jiangning; Manrong entered court as Outer Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can as Danyang governor made him Jiangning magistrate; he entered as Outer Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 昇明末，爲輔國長史、南海太守。

translations.literal: At the end of the Shengming era he was chief clerk to the Army of Assistance and Governor of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Shengming he was chief clerk to the Army of Assistance and Nanhai governor.

sentences.zh: 齊初，爲通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Early in Qi he was Regular Attendant and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Early Qi he was Regular Attendant and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 永明初，爲太子率更令，侍皇太子講。

translations.literal: Early in Yongming he was Director of the Crown Prince's Household and attended the crown prince's lectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early Yongming he directed the crown prince's household and attended his lectures.

sentences.zh: 衛將軍王儉深相交好，令與河內司馬憲、吳郡陸澄共撰《喪服義》，旣成，又欲與之定禮樂。

translations.literal: Guard General Wang Jian was deeply friendly with him and had him join Sima Xian of Henei and Lu Cheng of Wu commandery in compiling Explanations of Mourning Dress, and when that was done wished to fix rites and music with them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian befriended him and had him join Sima Xian and Lu Cheng to draft Explanations of Mourning Dress; when done Jian wished to fix rites and music with them.

sentences.zh: 會儉薨，遷中書侍郎、大司馬諮議參軍，出爲武昌太守。

translations.literal: When Jian died Manrong was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and staff adviser to the Grand Marshal, then went out as Governor of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Jian died; Manrong became Secretariat Gentleman and Grand Marshal staff adviser, then Wuchang governor.

sentences.zh: 建武中，入拜中散大夫。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era he entered as Palace Regular.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu he entered as Palace Regular.

sentences.zh: 時明帝不重儒術，曼容宅在瓦官寺東，施高坐於聽事，有賓客輒升高坐爲講說，生徒常數十百人。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Ming did not value Confucian learning; Manrong's house lay east of Waguan Temple, and in the reception hall he set a high seat—whenever guests came he mounted it to lecture, and pupils often numbered in the dozens or hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Ming did not esteem Confucianism; east of Waguan Temple Manrong set a high seat in his hall and lectured to dozens or hundreds of students.

sentences.zh: 梁臺建，以曼容舊儒，召拜司馬，出爲臨海太守。

translations.literal: When the Liang regime was being founded, as an old Confucian he was summoned as Marshal and went out as Governor of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang was founded he was summoned as Marshal as an elder scholar, then Linhai governor.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，卒官，時年八十二。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he died in office, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year one he died in office at eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 爲《周易》、《毛詩》、《喪服集解》、《老》、《莊》、《論語義》。

translations.literal: He wrote commentaries on the Book of Changes, Mao Odes, Collected Explanations of Mourning Dress, Laozi, Zhuangzi, and Explanations of the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote on the Changes, Mao Odes, mourning dress, Laozi, Zhuangzi, and the Analects.

sentences.zh: 子𣈶芃，在《良吏傳》。

translations.literal: His son Gao Peng appears in Biographies of Good Officials.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gao Peng is in Biographies of Good Officials.

sentences.zh: 何佟之

translations.literal: He Tongzhi
translations.idiomatic: He Tongzhi

sentences.zh: 何佟之字士威，廬江灊人，豫州刺史惲六世孫也。

translations.literal: He Tongzhi, courtesy name Shiwei, was a man of Qian in Lujiang, sixth-generation descendant of Regional Inspector Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He Tongzhi, styled Shiwei, of Qian in Lujiang, was sixth generation from Inspector Yun.

sentences.zh: 祖劭之，宋員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shao-zhi was Song Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shao-zhi was Song Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 父歆，齊奉朝請。

translations.literal: His father Xin was Qi Court Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin was Qi Court Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 佟之少好《三禮》，師心獨學，強力專精，手不輟卷，讀《禮》論二百篇，略皆上口。

translations.literal: Tongzhi in youth loved the Three Rites, studied with heart alone, was strong and wholly devoted, his hand never leaving the scroll; he read two hundred chapters of ritual discourse and could recite nearly all from memory.
translations.idiomatic: Young Tongzhi loved the Three Rites, studied alone with tireless devotion, read two hundred chapters of ritual discourse and could recite most by heart.

sentences.zh: 時太尉王儉爲時儒宗，雅相推重。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Marshal Wang Jian was the age's Confucian leader and greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Wang Jian, the age's Confucian leader, greatly esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 起家揚州從事，仍爲總明館學士，頻遷司徒車騎參軍事、尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: He first took office as Yangzhou staff member, then became a scholar at the Zongming Hall, and was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat and Cavalry staff officer and Director of the Ancestral Temples.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Yangzhou staff, became Zongming Hall scholar, and rose to Secretariat cavalry staff officer and Director of Ancestral Temples.

sentences.zh: 齊建武中，爲鎮北記室參軍，侍皇太子講，領丹陽邑中正。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era of Qi he was staff recorder to the Army of the North and attended the crown prince's lectures, holding the post of chief of the Danyang district.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Jianwu he was northern army recorder, attended crown prince lectures, and was Danyang district chief.

sentences.zh: 時步兵校尉劉瓛、徵士吳苞皆已卒，京邑碩儒，唯佟之而已。

translations.literal: At the time Infantry Commandant Liu Huan and Recluse Wu Bao had already died; among eminent Confucians of the capital only Tongzhi remained.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huan and Wu Bao were dead; in the capital only Tongzhi remained among great scholars.

sentences.zh: 佟之明習事數，當時國家吉凶禮則，皆取決焉，名重於世。

translations.literal: Tongzhi was clear and practiced in matters of number; at the time the state's auspicious and inauspicious ritual rules all took his decision, and his name weighed in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhi knew ritual detail; state rites for fortune and misfortune all followed his judgment, and his fame was great.

sentences.zh: 歷步兵校尉、國子博士，尋遷驃騎諮議參軍，轉司馬。

translations.literal: He served as Infantry Commandant and Erudite of the National University, then was promoted to staff adviser to the Rapid Cavalry General and transferred to Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was Infantry Commandant and university erudite, then rapid-cavalry staff adviser and marshal.

sentences.zh: 永元末，京師兵亂，佟之常集諸生講論，孜孜不怠。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongyuan, when the capital was in military turmoil, Tongzhi still gathered students to lecture and discuss, diligent and unwearying.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongyuan's end, amid capital turmoil, he still lectured students tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 中興初，拜驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Early in the Restoration he was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Restoration he became General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，尊重儒術，以佟之爲尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he honored Confucian learning and made Tongzhi Left Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu honored Confucianism and made him Left Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是時百度草創，佟之依《禮》定議，多所裨益。

translations.literal: At the time the hundred offices were newly founded; Tongzhi, following the Rites, settled decisions and contributed much.
translations.idiomatic: Offices were newly founded; Tongzhi settled many matters by the Rites.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，卒官，年五十五。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he died in office, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year two he died in office at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚悼惜，將贈之官；

translations.literal: Gaozu deeply mourned him and was about to confer posthumous office;
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu mourned him and meant to grant posthumous rank;

sentences.zh: 故事左丞無贈官者，特詔贈黃門侍郎，儒者榮之。

translations.literal: by precedent a left director received no posthumous appointment, but a special edict granted Yellow Gate Gentleman, to the glory of Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: left directors had no posthumous rank by precedent, but an edict made him Yellow Gate Gentleman—honor for scholars.

sentences.zh: 所著文章、《禮義》百許篇。

translations.literal: His writings—essays and ritual discourse—numbered over a hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He left over a hundred essays and ritual treatises.

sentences.zh: 子：朝隱、朝晦。

translations.literal: Sons: Chaoyin and Chaohui.
translations.idiomatic: Sons: Chaoyin and Chaohui.

sentences.zh: 范縝字子真，南鄉舞陰人也。

translations.literal: Fan Zhen, courtesy name Zizhen, was a man of Wuyang in Nanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen, styled Zizhen, was from Wuyang in Nanxiang.

sentences.zh: 晉安北將軍汪六世孫。

translations.literal: Sixth-generation descendant of Jin's General Who Pacifies the North Wang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixth generation from Jin General Who Pacifies the North Wang.

sentences.zh: 祖璩之，中書郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qu-zhi was Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qu-zhi was Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 父濛，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Meng died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Meng died young.

sentences.zh: 縝少孤貧，事母孝謹。

translations.literal: Zhen was orphaned young and poor, and served his mother with filial care.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he served his mother with filial care.

sentences.zh: 年未弱冠，聞沛國劉瓛聚衆講說。

translations.literal: Before he had reached the capping age he heard that Liu Huan of Pei commandery was gathering a crowd to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before capping age he heard Liu Huan of Pei was lecturing to a crowd.

sentences.zh: 始往從之，卓越不羣而勤學，瓛甚奇之，親爲之冠。

translations.literal: He first went to follow him—outstanding among the group yet diligent in study; Huan marveled at him and personally capped him.
translations.idiomatic: He went to study—stood out yet worked hard; Huan marveled and capped him himself.

sentences.zh: 在瓛門下積年，去來歸家，恒芒屩布衣，徒行于路。

translations.literal: He remained at Huan's gate for years, coming and going home, always in straw sandals and plain cloth, walking on foot along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Years at Huan's gate he went home in straw sandals and plain cloth, walking on foot.

sentences.zh: 瓛門多車馬貴遊，縝在其門，聊無恥愧。

translations.literal: Many at Huan's gate were chariots and noble travelers; Zhen in that company felt not the least shame.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's gate held carriages and nobles; Zhen among them felt no shame.

sentences.zh: 旣長，博通經術，尤精《三禮》。

translations.literal: When grown he was broadly versed in the classics, especially skilled in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he mastered the classics, especially the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 性質直，好危言高論，不爲士友所安。

translations.literal: His nature was upright; he loved stern words and lofty discourse and did not put his scholar friends at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Upright by nature, he loved sharp talk and lofty argument and unsettled his peers.

sentences.zh: 唯與外弟蕭琛相善，琛名曰口辯，每服縝簡詣。

translations.literal: Only with his cousin on his mother's side, Xiao Chen, was he close; Chen was famed for eloquence and always yielded to Zhen's terse phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: Only his maternal cousin Xiao Chen was close; Chen was famed for eloquence yet yielded to Zhen's brevity.

sentences.zh: 起家齊寧蠻主簿，累遷尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: He first took office as Registrar to the Pacifier of the Barbarians of Qi, and was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Qi Pacifier registrar and rose to Palace Secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 永明年中，與魏氏和親，歲通聘好，特簡才學之士，以爲行人。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era, when peace was made with Wei and yearly embassies were exchanged, men of talent and learning were specially chosen as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming, at peace with Wei and yearly embassies, the ablest scholars were chosen as envoys.

sentences.zh: 縝及從弟雲、蕭琛、琅邪顏幼明、河東裴昭明相繼將命，皆著名鄰國。

translations.literal: Zhen and his cousin Yun, Xiao Chen, Yan Youming of Langye, and Pei Zhaoming of Hedong in succession bore the mission, all famed in neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen, his cousin Yun, Xiao Chen, Yan Youming, and Pei Zhaoming served in turn and were famed abroad.

sentences.zh: 于時竟陵王子良盛招賓客，縝亦預焉。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Jingling Zi Liang greatly gathered guests, and Zhen also took part.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jingling Zi Liang gathered many guests, and Zhen was among them.

sentences.zh: 建武中，遷領軍長史。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era he was promoted to chief clerk of the Army of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu he became Palace Guard chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 出爲宜都太守，母憂去職，歸居於南州。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Yidu; when his mother died he left office and returned to live in the southern provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was Yidu governor; at his mother's death he left office and lived in the south.

sentences.zh: 義軍至，縝墨絰來迎。

translations.literal: When the righteous army arrived, Zhen came in black hemp mourning to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army came, Zhen came in hemp mourning to welcome it.

sentences.zh: 高祖與縝有西邸之舊，見之甚悅。

translations.literal: Gaozu and Zhen had old ties from the Western Lodge; seeing him he was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had Western Lodge ties with Zhen and was very pleased to see him.

sentences.zh: 及建康城平，以縝爲晉安太守，在郡清約，資公祿而已。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified he made Zhen Governor of Jin'an; in the commandery he was pure and frugal, living only on public salary.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang fell he made Zhen Jin'an governor; in office he was frugal and lived on salary alone.

sentences.zh: 視事四年，徵爲尚書左丞。

translations.literal: After four years in office he was summoned as Left Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he was recalled as Left Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 縝去還，雖親戚無所遺，唯餉前尚書令王亮。

translations.literal: When Zhen left and returned, though among kin he left nothing, he alone sent gifts to former Secretariat Director Wang Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving office he gave nothing to kin but sent gifts to former Director Wang Liang.

sentences.zh: 縝仕齊時，與亮同臺爲郎，舊相友，至是亮被擯棄在家。

translations.literal: When Zhen served in Qi he and Liang had been colleagues in the same office as gentlemen; they were old friends, and now Liang had been cast aside and was at home.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi he and Liang had been colleagues and friends; now Liang was dismissed at home.

sentences.zh: 縝自迎王師，志在權軸，旣而所懷未滿，亦常怏怏，故私相親結，以矯時云。

translations.literal: Zhen himself had welcomed the royal army and aimed at the hubs of power; when his hopes were not fulfilled he was often discontent, and so he privately drew close to Liang to set the times aright, as it were.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had welcomed the royal army hoping for high power; unfulfilled, he grew resentful and privately befriended Liang to rebalance the times.

sentences.zh: 後竟坐亮徙廣州，語在

translations.literal: Later he was ultimately implicated through Liang and exiled to Guangzhou; the account is in
translations.idiomatic: He was finally implicated with Liang and sent to Guangzhou; see

sentences.zh: 〈亮傳〉

translations.literal: Biography of Liang
translations.idiomatic: the Biography of Liang

sentences.zh: 初，縝在齊世，嘗侍竟陵王子良。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhen was in the Qi era, he had once attended Prince of Jingling Zi Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in Qi he had attended Prince of Jingling Zi Liang.

sentences.zh: 子良精信釋教，而縝盛稱無佛。

translations.literal: Zi Liang was deeply devoted to Buddhism, while Zhen strongly asserted there was no Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Liang deeply believed Buddhism; Zhen insisted there was no Buddha.

sentences.zh: 子良問曰：「君不信因果，世間何得有富貴，何得有貧賤？

translations.literal: Zi Liang asked: "If you do not believe in cause and effect, how can there be wealth and honor in the world, and how can there be poverty and low station?
translations.idiomatic: Zi Liang asked: "If you deny cause and effect, why are some rich and noble and others poor?

sentences.zh: 」縝答曰：「人之生譬如一樹花，同發一枝，俱開一蔕，隨風而墮，自有拂簾幌墜於茵席之上，自有關籬牆落於糞溷之側。

translations.literal: " Zhen answered: "Human birth is like flowers on one tree—they issue from one branch, open on one calyx, and fall with the wind; some brush the curtain and fall on cushions and mats, some pass the fence and fall beside the privy.
translations.idiomatic: "; Zhen answered: "Life is like flowers on one tree—same branch, same bud, wind-blown down; some land on cushions, some in the privy.

sentences.zh: 墜茵席者，殿下是也；

translations.literal: Those who fall on cushions and mats—that is Your Highness;
translations.idiomatic: Those on cushions—that is Your Highness;

sentences.zh: 落糞溷者，下官是也。

translations.literal: those who fall beside the privy—that is this humble office.
translations.idiomatic: those in the privy—that is me.

sentences.zh: 貴賤雖復殊途，因果竟在何處？

translations.literal: Though noble and base follow different paths, where indeed is cause and effect?
translations.idiomatic: Noble and base differ—but where is cause and effect?

sentences.zh: 」子良不能屈，深怪之。

translations.literal: " Zi Liang could not refute him and was deeply astonished.
translations.idiomatic: "; Zi Liang could not answer and was deeply struck.

sentences.zh: 縝退論其理，著《神滅論》曰：

translations.literal: Zhen withdrew and debated the principle, composing On the Annihilation of the Spirit, which says:
translations.idiomatic: Zhen withdrew, argued the point, and wrote On the Annihilation of the Spirit:

sentences.zh: 或問予云：「神滅，何以知其滅也？

translations.literal: Someone asked me: "If the spirit is annihilated, how do you know it is annihilated?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked: "If the spirit is destroyed, how do you know it is destroyed?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「神卽形也，形卽神也；

translations.literal: " I answered: "Spirit is form and form is spirit;
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "Spirit is form and form is spirit;

sentences.zh: 是以形存則神存，形謝則神滅也。」

translations.literal: therefore when form exists spirit exists; when form perishes spirit is annihilated."
translations.idiomatic: so when form exists spirit exists; when form ends spirit is destroyed."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「形者無知之稱，神者有知之名。

translations.literal: The questioner said: "Form is what is called without knowing; spirit is what is called with knowing.
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "Form is the name for the unknowing; spirit for the knowing.

sentences.zh: 知與無知，卽事有異，神之與形，理不容一，形神相卽，非所聞也。

translations.literal: Knowing and not knowing are different in the matter; spirit and form cannot share one principle—form and spirit as one has not been heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing and not knowing differ; spirit and form cannot be one—unity of form and spirit is unheard of.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「形者神之質，神者形之用；

translations.literal: " I answered: "Form is the substance of spirit; spirit is the function of form;
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "Form is spirit's substance; spirit is form's function;

sentences.zh: 是則形稱其質，神言其用；

translations.literal: thus form names its substance and spirit names its function;
translations.idiomatic: form names substance, spirit names function;

sentences.zh: 形之與神，不得相異也。」

translations.literal: form and spirit cannot differ."
translations.idiomatic: form and spirit cannot differ."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「神故非質，形故非用，不得爲異，其義安在？

translations.literal: The questioner said: "If spirit is not substance and form is not function, they cannot differ—where is the meaning?
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "If spirit is not substance and form not function, how can they not differ—what is the sense?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「名殊而體一也。」

translations.literal: " I answered: "The names differ but the body is one."
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "Names differ but the body is one."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「名旣已殊，體何得一？

translations.literal: The questioner said: "If the names are already different, how can the body be one?
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "If names differ, how is the body one?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「神之於質，猶利之於刀；

translations.literal: " I answered: "Spirit to substance is like sharpness to knife;
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "Spirit to substance is like sharpness to a knife;

sentences.zh: 形之於用，猶刀之於利；

translations.literal: form to function is like knife to sharpness;
translations.idiomatic: form to function is like the knife to sharpness;

sentences.zh: 利之名非刀也，刀之名非利也。

translations.literal: the name sharpness is not knife, and the name knife is not sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: sharpness is not the knife, and the knife is not sharpness.

sentences.zh: 然而捨利無刀，捨刀無利。

translations.literal: Yet abandon sharpness and there is no knife; abandon knife and there is no sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet without sharpness there is no knife; without knife no sharpness.

sentences.zh: 未聞刀沒而利存，豈容形亡而神在？」

translations.literal: One never hears that the knife is gone while sharpness remains—how could form perish while spirit remains?"
translations.idiomatic: No one hears of a knife gone while sharpness remains—how could form die while spirit stays?"

sentences.zh: 問曰：「刀之與利，或如來說；

translations.literal: The questioner said: "Knife and sharpness may be as you say;
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Knife and sharpness may be as you say;

sentences.zh: 形之與神，其義不然。

translations.literal: form and spirit are not so in meaning.
translations.idiomatic: but form and spirit are not the same.

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: Why do I say so?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 木之質無知也，人之質有知也；

translations.literal: The substance of wood is without knowing; the substance of man has knowing;
translations.idiomatic: Wood's substance has no knowing; man's has knowing;

sentences.zh: 人旣有如木之質，而有異木之知，豈非木有一、人有二邪？

translations.literal: if man has a substance like wood and also knowing unlike wood, is that not wood having one and man having two?
translations.idiomatic: if man has wood-like substance and unlike-wood knowing, does man have two where wood has one?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「異哉言乎！

translations.literal: " I answered: "Strange words indeed!
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "Strange words!

sentences.zh: 人若有如木之質以爲形，又有異木之知以爲神，則可如來論也。

translations.literal: If man had a wood-like substance as form and also unlike-wood knowing as spirit, then your argument could stand.
translations.idiomatic: If man had wood-like substance as form and unlike-wood knowing as spirit, your point might stand.

sentences.zh: 今人之質，質有知也；

translations.literal: Now man's substance has knowing;
translations.idiomatic: But man's substance has knowing;

sentences.zh: 木之質，質無知也。

translations.literal: wood's substance has no knowing.
translations.idiomatic: wood's has none.

sentences.zh: 人之質非木質也，木之質非人質也，安有如木之質而復有異木之知哉！」

translations.literal: Man's substance is not wood's substance, and wood's substance is not man's substance—how could there be wood-like substance and also unlike-wood knowing?"
translations.idiomatic: Man's substance is not wood's, nor wood's man's—how could there be wood-like substance with unlike-wood knowing?"

sentences.zh: 問曰：「人之質所以異木質者，以其有知耳。

translations.literal: The questioner said: "The reason man's substance differs from wood's is that he has knowing.
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "Man differs from wood because he has knowing.

sentences.zh: 人而無知，與木何異？

translations.literal: If man had no knowing, how would he differ from wood?
translations.idiomatic: Without knowing, how would he differ from wood?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「人無無知之質，猶木無有知之形。」

translations.literal: " I answered: "Man has no substance without knowing, just as wood has no form with knowing."
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "Man has no unknowing substance, as wood has no knowing form."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「死者之形骸，豈非無知之質邪？

translations.literal: The questioner said: "The corpse's frame—is it not a substance without knowing?
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "A corpse's frame—is that not unknowing substance?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「是無人質。」

translations.literal: " I answered: "That is substance without a person."
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "That is substance without a person."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「若然者，人果有如木之質，而有異木之知矣。

translations.literal: The questioner said: "If so, then man indeed has a wood-like substance and also unlike-wood knowing.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Then man has wood-like substance and unlike-wood knowing.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「死者如木，而無異木之知；

translations.literal: " I answered: "The dead are like wood and have no unlike-wood knowing;
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "The dead are like wood without unlike-wood knowing;

sentences.zh: 生者有異木之知，而無如木之質也。」

translations.literal: the living have unlike-wood knowing and no wood-like substance."
translations.idiomatic: the living have unlike-wood knowing without wood-like substance."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「死者之骨骼，非生之形骸邪？

translations.literal: The questioner said: "The dead person's bones—are they not the living person's frame?
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "Dead bones—are they not the living person's frame?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「生形之非死形，死形之非生形，區已革矣。

translations.literal: " I answered: "The living form is not the dead form; the dead form is not the living form—the distinction is already changed.
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "Living form is not dead form, dead not living—the distinction has changed.

sentences.zh: 安有生人之形骸，而有死人之骨骼哉？」

translations.literal: How could there be a living person's frame and also a dead person's bones?"
translations.idiomatic: How could one have a living frame and dead bones?"

sentences.zh: 問曰：「若生者之形骸，非死者之骨骼；

translations.literal: The questioner said: "If the living person's frame is not the dead person's bones,
translations.idiomatic: He said: "If the living frame is not dead bones,

sentences.zh: 非死者之骨骼，則應不由生者之形骸；

translations.literal: if it is not the dead person's bones, then it should not come from the living person's frame;
translations.idiomatic: then it should not come from the living frame;

sentences.zh: 不由生者之形骸，則此骨骼從何而至此邪？

translations.literal: if it does not come from the living person's frame, then from where did these bones arrive?
translations.idiomatic: if not from the living frame, whence these bones?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「是生者之形骸，變爲死者之骨骼也。」

translations.literal: " I answered: "It is the living person's frame transformed into the dead person's bones."
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "The living frame became the dead bones."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「生者之形骸雖變爲死者之骨骼，豈不因生而有死？

translations.literal: The questioner said: "Though the living person's frame changes into the dead person's bones, surely it is because there was life that there is death?
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "Though the living frame becomes dead bones, is death not from life?

sentences.zh: 則知死體猶生體也。

translations.literal: Then one knows the dead body is still the living body."
translations.idiomatic: Then the dead body is still the living body."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「如因榮木變爲枯木，枯木之質，甯是榮木之體！」

translations.literal: " I answered: "If it is like flourishing wood changing into withered wood, is the substance of withered wood still the body of flourishing wood?"
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "As flourishing wood becomes withered, is withered substance still flourishing body?"

sentences.zh: 問曰：「榮體變爲枯體，枯體卽是榮體；

translations.literal: The questioner said: "If the flourishing body changes into the withered body, the withered body is the flourishing body;
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Flourishing body becomes withered; withered is flourishing;

sentences.zh: 絲體變爲縷體，縷體卽是絲體，有何別焉？

translations.literal: if silk substance changes into thread substance, thread substance is silk substance—what difference is there?
translations.idiomatic: silk becomes thread; thread is silk—what difference?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「若枯卽是榮，榮卽是枯，應榮時凋零，枯時結實也。

translations.literal: " I answered: "If withered is flourishing and flourishing is withered, then in flourishing time it should wither, and in withering time it should bear fruit.
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "If withered is flourishing, flourishing should wither and withering bear fruit.

sentences.zh: 又榮木不應變爲枯木，以榮卽枯，無所復變也。

translations.literal: Moreover flourishing wood should not change into withered wood, for if flourishing is withered there is nothing further to change.
translations.idiomatic: Flourishing wood should not become withered if flourishing is withered—nothing left to change.

sentences.zh: 榮枯是一，何不先枯後榮？

translations.literal: Why not first wither and then flourish?
translations.idiomatic: Why not wither first, then flourish?

sentences.zh: 要先榮後枯，何也？

translations.literal: Why must it first flourish and then wither?
translations.idiomatic: Why must it flourish first, then wither?

sentences.zh: 絲縷之義，亦同此破。」

translations.literal: The meaning of silk and thread is the same refutation."
translations.idiomatic: Silk and thread fail the same way."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「生形之謝，便應豁然都盡。

translations.literal: The questioner said: "When the living form perishes, it ought at once to be wholly extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "When the living form ends, it should vanish at once.

sentences.zh: 何故方受死形，綿歷未已邪？

translations.literal: Why then, having just received the dead form, does it linger on without end?
translations.idiomatic: Why does the dead form linger on?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「生滅之體，要有其次故也。

translations.literal: " I answered: "Substances of birth and extinction must have their sequence for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "Birth and extinction have sequence for this reason.

sentences.zh: 夫歘而生者必歘而滅，漸而生者必漸而滅。

translations.literal: What is born in a flash must perish in a flash; what is born gradually must perish gradually.
translations.idiomatic: What is born suddenly perishes suddenly; what is born gradually perishes gradually.

sentences.zh: 歘而生者，飄驟是也；

translations.literal: What is born in a flash is like a gust of wind;
translations.idiomatic: Sudden birth is like a gust;

sentences.zh: 漸而生者，動植是也。

translations.literal: what is born gradually is like moving things and plants.
translations.idiomatic: gradual birth is like animals and plants.

sentences.zh: 有歘有漸，物之理也。」

translations.literal: Having flash and gradual is the principle of things."
translations.idiomatic: Flash and gradual are nature's law."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「形卽是神者，手等亦是邪？

translations.literal: The questioner said: "If form is spirit, are the hands also so?
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "If form is spirit, are the hands too?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「皆是神之分也。」

translations.literal: " I answered: "They are all portions of spirit."
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "All are portions of spirit."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「若皆是神之分，神旣能慮，手等亦應能慮也？

translations.literal: The questioner said: "If they are all portions of spirit, and spirit can deliberate, should the hands also be able to deliberate?
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "If all are spirit's portions and spirit deliberates, should hands deliberate too?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「手等亦應能有痛癢之知，而無是非之慮。」

translations.literal: " I answered: "The hands also ought to have knowing of pain and itch, but not deliberation of right and wrong."
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "Hands may know pain and itch but not right and wrong."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「知之與慮，爲一爲異？

translations.literal: The questioner said: "Are knowing and deliberation one or different?
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "Are knowing and deliberation one or two?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「知卽是慮。

translations.literal: " I answered: "Knowing is deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "Knowing is deliberation.

sentences.zh: 淺則爲知，深則爲慮。」

translations.literal: Shallow it is knowing; deep it is deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: Shallow is knowing; deep is deliberation."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「若爾，應有二慮；

translations.literal: The questioner said: "If so, there ought to be two deliberations;
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Then there should be two deliberations;

sentences.zh: 慮旣有二，神有二乎？

translations.literal: if deliberation has two, are there two spirits?
translations.idiomatic: if two deliberations, two spirits?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「人體惟一，神何得二。」

translations.literal: " I answered: "The human body is only one—how could spirit be two?"
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "The body is one—how could spirit be two?"

sentences.zh: 問曰：「若不得二，安有痛癢之知，復有是非之慮？

translations.literal: The questioner said: "If it cannot be two, how can there be knowing of pain and itch and also deliberation of right and wrong?
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "If not two, how both pain-itch knowing and right-wrong deliberation?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「如手足雖異，總爲一人。

translations.literal: " I answered: "As hands and feet differ yet together make one person.
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "Hands and feet differ yet are one person.

sentences.zh: 是非痛癢雖復有異，亦總爲一神矣。」

translations.literal: Right-wrong and pain-itch, though they differ again, are also altogether one spirit."
translations.idiomatic: Right-wrong and pain-itch differ yet are one spirit."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「是非之慮，不關手足，當關何處？

translations.literal: The questioner said: "Deliberation of right and wrong does not concern hands and feet—what should it concern?
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "Right-wrong deliberation is not in hands and feet—where then?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「是非之慮，心器所主。」

translations.literal: " I answered: "Deliberation of right and wrong is ruled by the organ of the heart."
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "Right-wrong deliberation is ruled by the heart organ."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「心器是五藏之心，非邪？

translations.literal: The questioner said: "The heart organ is the heart among the five viscera—is it not?
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "The heart organ is the heart among the five viscera, is it not?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「是也。」

translations.literal: " I answered: "It is."
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "Yes."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「五藏有何殊別，而心獨有是非之慮乎？

translations.literal: The questioner said: "What special difference among the five viscera makes the heart alone have deliberation of right and wrong?
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "Why should the heart alone deliberate right and wrong among the five viscera?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「七竅亦復何殊，而司用不均。」

translations.literal: " I answered: "The seven apertures also differ—why are their uses unequal?"
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "The seven apertures differ too—why are their uses unequal?"

sentences.zh: 問曰：「慮思無方，何以知是心器所主？

translations.literal: The questioner said: "Deliberative thought has no fixed place—how do you know it is ruled by the heart organ?
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "Thought has no fixed place—how know the heart rules it?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「五藏各有所司，無有能慮者，是以知心爲慮本。」

translations.literal: " I answered: "The five viscera each have their charge; none can deliberate—therefore one knows the heart is the root of deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "Each viscus has its charge; none deliberates—so the heart is deliberation's root."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「何不寄在眼等分中？

translations.literal: The questioner said: "Why not lodge it in the portion of the eyes and the like?
translations.idiomatic: He asked: "Why not lodge it in the eye's portion?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「若慮可寄於眼分，眼何故不寄於耳分邪？」

translations.literal: " I answered: "If deliberation could lodge in the eye's portion, why should the eye not lodge in the ear's portion?"
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "If deliberation lodged in the eye, why not the eye in the ear?"

sentences.zh: 問曰：「慮體無本，故可寄之於眼分；

translations.literal: The questioner said: "The substance of deliberation has no root, so it can lodge in the eye's portion;
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Deliberation has no root, so it can lodge in the eye;

sentences.zh: 眼自有本，不假寄於佗分也。

translations.literal: the eye has its own root and need not lodge in another portion."
translations.idiomatic: the eye has its own root and need not lodge elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「眼何故有本而慮無本；

translations.literal: " I answered: "Why should the eye have a root while deliberation has no root;
translations.idiomatic: "; I answered: "Why should the eye have a root while deliberation has none;

sentences.zh: 苟無本於我形，而可遍寄於異地。

translations.literal: If there were no root in my form, yet it could be lodged everywhere in other places.
translations.idiomatic: If thought had no root in one's form, it could lodge everywhere abroad.

sentences.zh: 亦可張甲之情，寄王乙之軀；

translations.literal: One might as well lodge Zhang Jia's feelings in Wang Yi's body;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's mind could lodge in Wang's body;

sentences.zh: 李丙之性，託趙丁之體。

translations.literal: and Li Bing's nature in Zhao Ding's frame.
translations.idiomatic: and Li Bing's nature in Zhao Ding's frame.

sentences.zh: 然乎哉？

translations.literal: Is it so?
translations.idiomatic: Could that be?

sentences.zh: 不然也。」

translations.literal: It is not so."
translations.idiomatic: It is not so."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「聖人形猶凡人之形，而有凡聖之殊，故知形神異矣。

translations.literal: Question: "Sages' forms are like ordinary men's forms, yet there is ordinary and sage distinction—thus form and spirit differ."
translations.idiomatic: Question: "Sages look like ordinary men, yet sage and commoner differ—so body and soul must differ."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Answer: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Answer: "Not so.

sentences.zh: 金之精者能昭，穢者不能昭，有能昭之精金，寧有不昭之穢質。

translations.literal: Refined gold can shine; dross cannot shine—if there is refined gold that can shine, how could there be dross that does not shine?
translations.idiomatic: Fine gold shines; base ore does not—given shining fine gold, can there be non-shining dross?

sentences.zh: 又豈有聖人之神而寄凡人之器，亦無凡人之神而托聖人之體。

translations.literal: How could a sage's spirit lodge in an ordinary man's vessel, or an ordinary man's spirit lodge in a sage's frame?
translations.idiomatic: How could a sage's soul inhabit a commoner's body, or a commoner's soul a sage's?

sentences.zh: 是以八采、重瞳，勛、華之容；

translations.literal: Hence eight-colored regalia and double pupils—the countenances of Yao and Shun;
translations.idiomatic: Hence eight hues and double pupils—the faces of Yao and Shun;

sentences.zh: 龍顏、馬口，軒、皞之狀；

translations.literal: dragon face and horse mouth—the forms of Xuanyuan and Shaohao;
translations.idiomatic: dragon face and horse mouth—the looks of the Yellow Emperor and Shaohao;

sentences.zh: 形表之異也。

translations.literal: these are differences of outward form.
translations.idiomatic: these are outward differences.

sentences.zh: 比干之心，七竅列角；

translations.literal: Bi Gan's heart with seven openings arrayed like horns;
translations.idiomatic: Bi Gan's heart, seven openings like horns;

sentences.zh: 伯約之膽，其大若拳；

translations.literal: Jiang Wei's gall, large as a fist;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei's gall, big as a fist;

sentences.zh: 此心器之殊也。

translations.literal: these are differences of heart and vessel.
translations.idiomatic: these are inner differences.

sentences.zh: 是知聖人定分，每絕常區，非惟道革羣生，乃亦形超萬有。

translations.literal: Thus one knows sages' allotted stations each transcend the common run—not only does the Way transform the masses, their forms also surpass all things.
translations.idiomatic: Sages' stations transcend the ordinary—not only transforming the people but surpassing all in form.

sentences.zh: 凡聖均體，所未敢安。」

translations.literal: That sage and commoner share the same body—I dare not accept."
translations.idiomatic: That sage and commoner share one body—I cannot accept."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「子云聖人之形必異於凡者。

translations.literal: Question: "You say a sage's form must differ from an ordinary man's.
translations.idiomatic: Question: "You say sages' forms must differ from ordinary men's.

sentences.zh: 敢問陽貨類仲尼，項籍似大舜；

translations.literal: May I ask: Yang Huo resembled Zhongni, Xiang Yu resembled great Shun;
translations.idiomatic: Consider Yang Huo like Zhongni, Xiang Yu like great Shun;

sentences.zh: 舜、項、孔、陽，智革形同，其故何邪？

translations.literal: Shun, Xiang, Kong, and Yang—wisdom differed yet forms were alike; what is the reason?"
translations.idiomatic: yet Shun, Xiang, Kong, and Yang differed in wisdom though alike in form—why?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「珉似玉而非玉，雞類鳳而非鳳；

translations.literal: Answer: "Min stone resembles jade but is not jade; a cock resembles a phoenix but is not a phoenix;
translations.idiomatic: Answer: "Min stone looks like jade but is not jade; a cock like a phoenix but not a phoenix;

sentences.zh: 物誠有之，人故宜爾。

translations.literal: things truly have such cases; among men it is likewise fitting."
translations.idiomatic: such things exist in nature; among men it is the same."

sentences.zh: 項、陽貌似而非實似，心器不均，雖貌無益。」

translations.literal: Xiang and Yang resembled in appearance but not in reality; heart and vessel were unequal—though the face matched, it availed nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang and Yang looked alike but were not truly alike; unequal inner endowment made likeness useless."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「凡聖之殊，形器不一，可也。

translations.literal: Question: "That sage and commoner differ and vessels of form are not one—acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Question: "Sage and commoner may differ in form—that is fine.

sentences.zh: 聖人員極，理無有二；

translations.literal: Sages reach the ultimate; principle admits no twain;
translations.idiomatic: Sages reach the ultimate; principle has no second;

sentences.zh: 而丘、旦殊姿，湯、文異狀，神不侔色，於此益明矣。

translations.literal: yet Qiu and Dan had different looks, Tang and Wen different forms—spirit does not match appearance; here it is still clearer."
translations.idiomatic: yet Confucius and the Duke of Zhou differed in looks, Tang and Wen in form—soul does not match face; this is clearer still."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「聖同於心器，形不必同也，猶馬殊毛而齊逸，玉異色而均美。

translations.literal: Answer: "Sages are alike in heart and vessel; forms need not be alike—just as horses differ in hair yet equal in speed, jades differ in color yet equal in beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Answer: "Sages share heart and vessel; forms need not match—as horses differ in coat yet run alike, jades in hue yet equal in worth.

sentences.zh: 是以晉棘、荊和，等價連城；

translations.literal: Hence Jin Thorn and Jing He—equal price for cities chained together;
translations.idiomatic: Hence Jin Thorn and Jing He—worth a chain of cities;

sentences.zh: 驊騮、騄驪，俱致千里。」

translations.literal: Hualiu and Lüer—both reach a thousand li."
translations.idiomatic: Hualiu and Lüer—both run a thousand li."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「形神不二，旣聞之矣，形謝神滅，理固宜然。

translations.literal: Question: "Form and spirit are not two—I have heard that; when form decays spirit perishes—reason surely requires it.
translations.idiomatic: Question: "Body and soul are one—I accept that; when the body fails the soul ends—as reason demands.

sentences.zh: 敢問經云『爲之宗廟，以鬼饗之』，何謂也？

translations.literal: May I ask: the classic says 'Make for him an ancestral temple, to feed him as a ghost'—what does it mean?"
translations.idiomatic: But the classic says, 'Make ancestral temples and feed them as ghosts'—what does that mean?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「聖人之教然也。

translations.literal: Answer: "It is the sage's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Answer: "It is the sage's teaching.

sentences.zh: 所以弭孝子之心，而厲偷薄之意，神而明之，此之謂矣。」

translations.literal: Thus to soothe the filial son's heart and to sharpen the lax and mean in intent—'spirit' made manifest: that is what is meant."
translations.idiomatic: It soothes filial hearts and rebukes lax conduct—'spirit' made clear: that is all."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「伯有被甲，彭生豕見，墳素著其事，寧是設教而已邪？

translations.literal: Question: "Bo You wore armor, Peng Sheng appeared as a pig—the histories record these matters; can they be mere didactic devices?"
translations.idiomatic: Question: "Bo You in armor, Peng Sheng as a pig—histories record them; mere teaching devices?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「妖怪茫茫，或存或亡，強死者衆，不皆爲鬼。

translations.literal: Answer: "Strange apparitions are vast and dim—sometimes present, sometimes gone; many die by violence yet not all become ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: Answer: "Strange things are dim—now here, now gone; many violent deaths do not all become ghosts.

sentences.zh: 彭生、伯有，何獨能然；

translations.literal: Peng Sheng and Bo You—why alone could they do so?
translations.idiomatic: Why should Peng Sheng and Bo You alone do so?

sentences.zh: 乍爲人豕，未必齊、鄭之公子也。」

translations.literal: Suddenly becoming a man or a pig—not necessarily the lords of Qi and Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: Turning into man or pig—not necessarily Qi and Zheng's princes."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「《易》稱『故知鬼神之情狀，與天地相似而不違』。

translations.literal: Question: "The Changes says, 'Thus one knows the ghosts' and spirits' conditions, similar to Heaven and Earth and not at odds with them.'
translations.idiomatic: Question: "The Changes says one may know ghosts' and spirits' states, akin to Heaven and Earth without conflict."

sentences.zh: 又曰：『載鬼一車。

translations.literal: It also says: 'A cartload of ghosts.'
translations.idiomatic: It also says, 'A cartload of ghosts.'

sentences.zh: 』其義云何？

translations.literal: What is the meaning?"
translations.idiomatic: What does that mean?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「有禽焉，有獸焉，飛走之別也；

translations.literal: Answer: "There are birds and there are beasts—the distinction of flying and running;
translations.idiomatic: Answer: "There are birds and beasts—the flying and walking kinds;

sentences.zh: 有人焉，有鬼焉，幽明之別也。

translations.literal: there are men and there are ghosts—the distinction of dark and bright.
translations.idiomatic: there are men and ghosts—the living and the dead.

sentences.zh: 人滅而爲鬼，鬼滅而爲人，則未之知也。」

translations.literal: Man perishing to become ghost, ghost perishing to become man—I have not yet known it."
translations.idiomatic: Men becoming ghosts, ghosts becoming men—that I do not know."

sentences.zh: 問曰：「知此神滅，有何利用邪？

translations.literal: Question: "Knowing this spirit perishes—what use is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Question: "Knowing the soul perishes—what is the use?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「浮屠害政，桑門蠹俗。

translations.literal: Answer: "The Buddha harms government; clerics corrupt custom.
translations.idiomatic: Answer: "Buddhism harms rule; monks corrupt custom.

sentences.zh: 風驚霧起，馳蕩不休。

translations.literal: Wind startles and mist rises—they rush and swirl without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Winds rise and mists swirl—they rush on endlessly.

sentences.zh: 吾哀其弊，思拯其溺。

translations.literal: I pity their harm and wish to save the drowning.
translations.idiomatic: I pity the harm and would save the drowning.

sentences.zh: 夫竭財以赴僧，破產以趨佛，而不卹親戚，不憐窮匱者何？

translations.literal: Why do men exhaust wealth to attend monks, ruin estates to hurry to Buddha, yet not care for kin and not pity the poor and destitute?
translations.idiomatic: Why exhaust wealth on monks, ruin estates for Buddha, yet neglect kin and pity no poor?

sentences.zh: 良由厚我之情深，濟物之意淺。

translations.literal: Truly because feeling for self runs deep and intent to aid things runs shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Because love of self runs deep and care for others runs shallow.

sentences.zh: 是以圭撮涉於貧友，吝情動於顏色；

translations.literal: Hence a cup or spoon for a poor friend—stingy feeling shows in the face;
translations.idiomatic: A cup for a poor friend brings a stingy face;

sentences.zh: 千鐘委於富僧，歡意暢於容發。

translations.literal: a thousand zhong given to a rich monk—joy shows in the expression.
translations.idiomatic: a thousand zhong to a rich monk brings a bright face.

sentences.zh: 豈不以僧有多稌之期，友無遺秉之報，務施闕於周急，歸德必於在己。

translations.literal: Is it not because monks promise many harvests while friends offer no leftover sheaf in return—urgent aid is neglected while merit must return to oneself?
translations.idiomatic: Monks promise harvests; friends offer no return—aid in need is skimped while merit must accrue to oneself.

sentences.zh: 又惑以茫昧之言，懼以阿鼻之苦，誘以虛誕之辭，欣以兜率之樂。

translations.literal: They are also deluded by dim vague words, frightened by Avici torment, enticed by empty false phrases, delighted by Tusita joy.
translations.idiomatic: Dim words delude them, Avici frightens, false tales entice, Tusita delights.

sentences.zh: 故捨逢掖，襲橫衣，廢俎豆，列缾缽；

translations.literal: Hence they cast off wide sleeves, don cross-robe, abandon meat and grain stands, array alms bowls;
translations.idiomatic: They cast off scholar robes, don monks' garb, abandon ritual vessels, take up begging bowls;

sentences.zh: 家家棄其親愛，人人絕其嗣續。

translations.literal: every household abandons those it loves; every man cuts off his line.
translations.idiomatic: households abandon kin; men end their lines.

sentences.zh: 致使兵挫於行間，吏空於官府，粟罄於惰遊，貨殫於泥木。

translations.literal: Hence troops fail in the ranks, offices stand empty, grain is spent on idlers, goods exhausted on clay and wood.
translations.idiomatic: Armies weaken, offices empty, grain spent on idlers, wealth on idols.

sentences.zh: 所以姦宄弗勝，頌聲尚擁，惟此之故，其流莫已，其病無限。

translations.literal: Thus villains are not overcome yet praise still crowds—only for this cause: the current never stops; the disease has no limit.
translations.idiomatic: Villains thrive while praise abounds—for this the flood never ends and the disease has no limit.

sentences.zh: 若陶甄稟于自然，森羅均於獨化；

translations.literal: If pottery and casting receive from nature and the forested myriad are equal in spontaneous transformation;
translations.idiomatic: If all things arise from nature and transform alike;

sentences.zh: 忽焉自有，恍爾而無，來也不禦，去也不追，乘夫天理，各安其性。

translations.literal: suddenly they exist, dimly they vanish; coming cannot be barred, going cannot be pursued—riding Heaven's principle, each rests in its nature.
translations.idiomatic: suddenly present, dimly gone; coming unbarred, going unchased—each rests in its nature by Heaven's law.

sentences.zh: 小人甘其壟畝，君子保其恬素；

translations.literal: The petty man is content with his furrow; the gentleman keeps his plain simplicity;
translations.idiomatic: Petty men content with fields; gentlemen keep plain simplicity;

sentences.zh: 耕而食，食不可窮也；

translations.literal: plowing to eat—food cannot be exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: plow to eat—food never runs out;

sentences.zh: 蠶而衣，衣不可盡也；

translations.literal: silkworms to clothe—clothing cannot be used up;
translations.idiomatic: raise silkworms to clothe—cloth never runs out;

sentences.zh: 下有餘以奉其上，上無爲以待其下，可以全生，可以匡國，可以霸君，用此道也。」

translations.literal: below has surplus to serve above; above is non-active to await below—by this one can preserve life, rectify the state, and make a lord hegemon: use this Way."
translations.idiomatic: the lower has surplus for the upper; the upper is inactive awaiting the lower—life preserved, state rectified, hegemony won: this is the Way."

sentences.zh: 此論出，朝野喧嘩，子良集僧難之而不能屈。

translations.literal: When this treatise appeared court and countryside clamored; Ziliang gathered monks to refute it but could not bend him.
translations.idiomatic: When the essay appeared court and country clamored; Ziliang gathered monks to challenge him but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 縝在南累年，追還京。

translations.literal: Zhen remained in the south many years, then was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen stayed in the south many years, then was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 旣至，以爲中書郎、國子博士，卒官。

translations.literal: When he arrived he was made Secretariat Gentleman and Erudite of the National University and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he became Secretariat Gentleman and National University erudite and died in office.

sentences.zh: 文集十卷。

translations.literal: Collected writings in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to ten juan.

sentences.zh: 子胥，字長才。

translations.literal: His son Xu, styled Changcai.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu, styled Changcai.

sentences.zh: 傳父學，起家太學博士。

translations.literal: He inherited his father's learning and first took office as Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's learning and began as Imperial University erudite.

sentences.zh: 胥有口辯，大同中，常兼主客郎，對接北使。

translations.literal: Xu had eloquence; in the Datong era he often concurrently served as Master of Guests and received northern envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was eloquent; in Datong he often doubled as Master of Guests receiving northern envoys.

sentences.zh: 遷平西湘東王諮議參軍，侍宣城王讀。

translations.literal: He was promoted Adviser to the Prince of Xiangdong of Pacifying West and attended the Prince of Xuancheng in study.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Adviser to Pacifying West's Prince of Xiangdong and tutored the Prince of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 出爲鄱陽內史，卒於郡。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Poyang and died in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Poyang and died in office.

sentences.zh: 嚴植之

translations.literal: Yan Zhizhi
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhizhi

sentences.zh: 嚴植之字孝源，建平秭歸人也。

translations.literal: Yan Zhizhi, styled Xiaoyuan, was a man of Zigui in Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhizhi, styled Xiaoyuan, was from Zigui in Jianping.

sentences.zh: 祖欽，宋通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qin was Song Regular Attendant and Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qin was Song Regular Attendant and Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 植之少善《莊》、《老》，能玄言，精解《喪服》、《孝經》、《論語》。

translations.literal: Zhizhi in youth was skilled in Zhuangzi and Laozi, could speak arcane words, and had penetrating understanding of the Mourning Dress, Classic of Filial Piety, and Analects.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he mastered Zhuangzi and Laozi, spoke arcane doctrine, and excelled in Mourning Dress, Filial Piety, and Analects.

sentences.zh: 及長，遍治鄭氏《禮》、《周易》、《毛詩》、《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: When grown he thoroughly studied the Zheng clan Rites, Book of Changes, Mao Odes, and Zuo's Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he mastered Zheng Rites, Changes, Mao Odes, and Zuo's Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 性淳孝謹厚，不以所長高人。

translations.literal: His nature was pure, filial, careful, and thick; he did not set himself above others by his strengths.
translations.idiomatic: Pure, filial, and modest, he did not lord his learning over others.

sentences.zh: 少遭父憂，因菜食二十三載，後得風冷疾，乃止。

translations.literal: In youth he suffered his father's death and therefore ate only vegetables for twenty-three years; later he contracted wind-cold illness and only then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his father with vegetable fare for twenty-three years until wind-cold illness made him stop.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，始起家爲廬陵王國侍郎，遷廣漢王國右常侍。

translations.literal: In Qi's Yongming era he first took office as Gentleman of the Kingdom of Luling, then was transferred Right Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of Guanghan.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Yongming he began as Luling kingdom gentleman, then Guanghan Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 王誅，國人莫敢視，植之獨奔哭，手營殯殮，徒跣送喪墓所，爲起塚，葬畢乃還，當時義之。

translations.literal: When the prince was executed none in the state dared look on the corpse; Zhizhi alone ran to weep, with his own hands arranged encoffining, went barefoot to escort the bier to the grave, raised a mound, and only after burial returned—men of the time praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was killed none dared view the body; Zhizhi alone wept, encoffined him, went barefoot to the grave, raised a mound, and returned—men praised his duty.

sentences.zh: 建武中，遷員外郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era he was promoted Outer Gentleman and Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu he became Outer Gentleman and Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 尋爲康樂侯相，在縣清白，民吏稱之。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Marquis of Kangle's Chancellor; in the district he was pure and white, and people and officials praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Marquis of Kangle's chancellor; his rule was pure and officials and people praised him.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，板後軍騎兵參軍事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he was commissioned Cavalry Command Staff Officer in the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year two he was commissioned Rear Army cavalry staff officer.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔求通儒治五禮，有司奏植之治凶禮。

translations.literal: Gaozu edicted to seek comprehensive scholars to compile the Five Rites; the relevant offices memorialized that Zhizhi should handle mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sought scholars for the Five Rites; the offices named Zhizhi for mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 四年初，置《五經》博士，各開館教授，以植之兼《五經》博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the fourth year Erudites of the Five Classics were established, each opening a hall to teach; Zhizhi was made concurrent Erudite of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Five Classics erudites were set up; Zhizhi was made concurrent erudite.

sentences.zh: 植之館在潮溝，生徒常百數。

translations.literal: Zhizhi's hall was at Chaogou; pupils often numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: His hall at Chaogou usually had hundreds of pupils.

sentences.zh: 植之講，五館生必至，聽者千餘人。

translations.literal: When Zhizhi lectured, pupils of all five halls had to attend—listeners exceeded a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When he lectured, all five halls attended—over a thousand listeners.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷中撫軍記室參軍，猶兼博士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted Staff Officer to the Pacifying Center Army, still concurrently erudite.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he became Pacifying Center Army staff officer, still erudite.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒于館，時年五十二。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died in the hall, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he died in the hall at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 植之自疾後，便不受廩俸，妻子困乏。

translations.literal: After his illness Zhizhi would not accept salary grain; wife and children were in want.
translations.idiomatic: After illness he refused salary; his wife and children were destitute.

sentences.zh: 旣卒，喪無所寄，生徒爲市宅，乃得成喪焉。

translations.literal: After death there was nowhere for the funeral; pupils bought a house so the rites could be completed.
translations.idiomatic: After death there was no home for the funeral; pupils bought a house to complete the rites.

sentences.zh: 植之性仁慈，好行陰德，雖在闇室，未嘗怠也。

translations.literal: Zhizhi's nature was benevolent and kind; he loved to perform hidden virtue—even in a dark room he never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolent by nature, he did hidden good and never slackened even alone.

sentences.zh: 少嘗山行，見一患者，植之問其姓名，不能答，載與俱歸，爲營醫藥，六日而死。

translations.literal: In youth once on a mountain walk he saw a sick man; Zhizhi asked his name but he could not answer; he carried him home, provided medicine, and after six days the man died.
translations.idiomatic: Once on a mountain path he found a sick man who could not speak his name; he took him home, gave medicine, and he died in six days.

sentences.zh: 植之爲棺殮殯之，卒不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Zhizhi coffined and buried him; in the end he never knew where the man was from.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi coffined and buried him, never learning who he was.

sentences.zh: 嘗緣柵塘行，見患人臥塘側，植之下車問其故，云姓黃氏，家本荊州，爲人傭賃，疾旣危篤，船主將發，棄之于岸。

translations.literal: Once walking along the Zhazha embankment he saw a sick man lying beside the pond; Zhizhi left the carriage and asked the reason. The man said his surname was Huang, his family was originally from Jingzhou, he had been hired as a laborer, his illness was already critical, the boat master was about to depart, and he had been abandoned on the bank.
translations.idiomatic: By Zhazha pond he found a sick Huang from Jingzhou, a hired laborer abandoned on the bank as the boat was leaving.

sentences.zh: 植之心惻然，載還治之，經年而黃氏差，請終身充奴僕以報厚恩。

translations.literal: Zhizhi's heart was moved with pity; he carried him back and treated him. After a year Huang recovered and asked to serve as slave for life to repay the great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi took him in and cured him; Huang offered lifelong service in thanks.

sentences.zh: 植之不受，遺以資糧，遣之。

translations.literal: Zhizhi would not accept it but gave him provisions and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi refused, gave him supplies, and sent him off.

sentences.zh: 其義行多如此。

translations.literal: His righteous conduct was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His righteous deeds were mostly like this.

sentences.zh: 撰《凶禮儀注》四百七十九卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Rites Notes on Mourning in 479 juan.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Rites Notes on Mourning in 479 juan.

sentences.zh: 賀瑒字德璉，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: He Yang, styled Delian, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He Yang, styled Delian, was from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 祖道力，善《三禮》，仕宋爲尚書三公郎、建康令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Daoli was skilled in the Three Rites and served Song as Gentleman of the Three Dukes in the Secretariat and Magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Daoli mastered the Three Rites and served Song as Secretariat Three-Dukes Gentleman and Jiankang magistrate.

sentences.zh: 瑒少傳家業。

translations.literal: Yang in youth inherited the family profession.
translations.idiomatic: Yang in youth inherited the family learning.

sentences.zh: 齊時，沛國劉瓛爲會稽府丞，見瑒深器異之。

translations.literal: In Qi times Liu Huan of Pei was Assistant Administrator of Kuaiji; seeing Yang he deeply valued and regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi, Pei's Liu Huan as Kuaiji assistant deeply valued him.

sentences.zh: 嘗與俱造吳郡張融，指瑒謂融曰：「此生神明聰敏，將來當爲儒者宗。

translations.literal: Once he went with him to visit Zhang Rong of Wu commandery; pointing at Yang he said to Rong: "This lad is bright and keen; in future he will be patriarch of the Ru."
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Wu's Zhang Rong with him, he said, "This youth is bright; he will head the Confucians."

sentences.zh: 」瓛還，薦之爲國子生。

translations.literal: Huan returned and recommended him as a National University student.
translations.idiomatic: Huan returned and recommended him as National University student.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，揚州祭酒，俄兼國子助教。

translations.literal: He was recommended on the Classics Examinations, made Libationer of Yangzhou, and soon concurrently National University Assistant Instructor.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended on the Classics, he became Yangzhou Libationer, then National University assistant instructor.

sentences.zh: 歷奉朝請、太學博士、太常丞，遭母憂去職。

translations.literal: He passed through Regular Attendant, Erudite of the Imperial University, and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he left office on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Regular Attendant, Imperial University erudite, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices vice director, then left for mourning.

sentences.zh: 天監初，復爲太常丞，有司舉治賓禮，召見說《禮》義，高祖異之，詔朝朔望，預華林講。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he again became Vice Director; the relevant offices recommended him to handle guest rites; summoned to audience he expounded ritual meaning—Gaozu was struck and edicted that he attend court on the first and fifteenth and join the Hualin lectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian he returned as vice director, was recommended for guest rites, expounded ritual to Gaozu, who had him attend on new and full moon and join Hualin lectures.

sentences.zh: 四年初，開五館，以瑒兼《五經》博士，別詔爲皇太子定禮，撰《五經義》。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the fourth year the five halls were opened; Yang was made concurrent Erudite of the Five Classics; by separate edict he fixed rites for the Crown Prince and compiled Meanings of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: In year four the five halls opened; Yang became concurrent erudite, fixed the crown prince's rites, and compiled Five Classics meanings.

sentences.zh: 瑒悉禮舊事。

translations.literal: Yang knew all old ritual matters.
translations.idiomatic: Yang knew all old ritual precedents.

sentences.zh: 時高祖方創定禮樂，瑒所建議，多見施行。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu was just establishing rites and music; Yang's proposals were mostly put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: As Gaozu was establishing rites and music, most of Yang's proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 七年，拜步兵校尉，領《五經》博士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers and led as Erudite of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he became Commandant of Footsoldiers and led as Five Classics erudite.

sentences.zh: 九年，遇疾，遣醫藥省問，卒于館，時年五十九。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he fell ill; medicine and inquiries were sent; he died in the hall, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he fell ill; the court sent medicine; he died in the hall at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 所著《禮》、《易》、《老》、《莊講疏》、《朝廷博議》數百篇，《賓禮儀注》一百四十五卷。

translations.literal: His works included several hundred items of Exegeses on Rites, Changes, Laozi, and Zhuangzi, Court Deliberations, and Guest Rites Notes in 145 juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote hundreds of exegeses on Rites, Changes, Laozi, and Zhuangzi, court deliberations, and Guest Rites Notes in 145 juan.

sentences.zh: 瑒于《禮》尤精，館中生徒常百數，弟子明經封策至數十人。

translations.literal: Yang was especially expert in Rites; hall pupils often numbered in the hundreds; disciples who passed the Classics Examinations and court answers reached several tens.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in Rites; his hall had hundreds of pupils and dozens who passed examinations.

sentences.zh: 二子。

translations.literal: Two sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons.

sentences.zh: 革，字文明。

translations.literal: Ge, styled Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: Ge, styled Wenming.

sentences.zh: 少通《三禮》，及長，遍治《孝經》、《論語》、《毛詩》、《左傳》。
