translations.literal: In youth he mastered the Three Rites; when grown he thoroughly studied the Classic of Filial Piety, Analects, Mao Odes, and Zuo Tradition.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he mastered the Three Rites; grown, he mastered Filial Piety, Analects, Mao Odes, and Zuo.

sentences.zh: 起家晉安王國侍郎、兼太學博士，侍湘東王讀。

translations.literal: He first took office as Gentleman of the Kingdom of Jin'an and concurrent Erudite of the Imperial University, attending the Prince of Xiangdong in study.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Jin'an kingdom gentleman and concurrent Imperial University erudite, tutoring the Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 敕於永福省爲邵陵、湘東、武陵三王講禮。

translations.literal: By edict at Yongfu Palace he lectured on Rites for the three princes of Shaoling, Xiangdong, and Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: By edict at Yongfu Palace he taught Rites to the princes of Shaoling, Xiangdong, and Wuling.

sentences.zh: 稍遷湘東王府行參軍，轉尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted Staff Officer in the Prince of Xiangdong's kingdom and transferred Gentleman of Ritual Protocol in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Xiangdong staff officer, then Secretariat Ritual Protocol gentleman.

sentences.zh: 尋除秣陵令，遷國子博士，于學講授，生徒常數百人。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed as Magistrate of Moling, promoted Erudite of the National University; at the academy he lectured and pupils often numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Moling magistrate, then National University erudite lecturing to hundreds.

sentences.zh: 出爲西中郎湘東王諮議參軍，帶江陵令。

translations.literal: He went out as Adviser to the Western Center Army's Prince of Xiangdong, concurrently Magistrate of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He became Western Center Army adviser to the Prince of Xiangdong, concurrently Jiangling magistrate.

sentences.zh: 王初於府置學，以革領儒林祭酒，講《三禮》，荊楚衣冠聽者甚衆。

translations.literal: When the prince first established a school in the headquarters, Ge was made Libationer of the Confucian Grove, lecturing on the Three Rites; gentry of Jing and Chu who listened were very many.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince opened a school, Ge led as Confucian Grove libationer lecturing the Three Rites to many Jing-Chu gentry.

sentences.zh: 前後再監南平郡，爲民吏所德。

translations.literal: Before and after he twice supervised Nanping commandery and was esteemed by people and officials.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he supervised Nanping and won officials' and people's esteem.

sentences.zh: 尋加貞威將軍、兼平西長史、南郡太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally Trustworthy Might General, concurrently Chief Clerk of Pacifying West, and Administrator of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he added Trustworthy Might General, Pacifying West chief clerk, and Nan commandery administrator.

sentences.zh: 革性至孝，常恨貪祿代耕，不及養。

translations.literal: Ge's nature was utmost filial; he often regretted that receiving salary in place of plowing left him unable to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Utterly filial, he regretted that salary replaced farming and he could not nourish his parents.

sentences.zh: 在荊州歷爲郡縣，所得俸秩，不及妻孥，專擬還鄉造寺，以申感思。

translations.literal: In Jingzhou he successively served as commandery and county official; the salary he received did not reach wife and children—he planned only to return home to build a temple to express grateful remembrance.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingzhou his salary never reached his family; he meant to return home and build a temple in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 大同六年，卒官，時年六十二。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Datong he died in office, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year six he died in office at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 弟季，亦明《三禮》，歷官尚書祠部郎，兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ji was also expert in the Three Rites; he passed through Gentleman of the Imperial Ancestral Temples in the Secretariat and concurrent Secretariat Attendant for General Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Ji also mastered the Three Rites and served as Temples gentleman and Secretariat attendant for general affairs.

sentences.zh: 累遷步兵校尉、中書黃門郎，兼著作。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession Commandant of Footsoldiers, Secretariat Yellow Gate Gentleman, and concurrently Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Commandant of Footsoldiers, Yellow Gate gentleman, and compiler.

sentences.zh: 司馬筠

translations.literal: Sima Jun
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jun

sentences.zh: 司馬筠字貞素，河內溫人，晉驃騎將軍譙烈王承七世孫。

translations.literal: Sima Jun, styled Zhensu, was a man of Wen in Henei, seventh-generation descendant of Jin General of Agile Cavalry and Prince of Qiao Lie Wang Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jun, styled Zhensu, of Wen in Henei, was seventh generation from Jin General of Agile Cavalry Prince of Qiao Lie Wang Cheng.

sentences.zh: 祖亮，宋司空從事中郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Liang was Song Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Liang was Song vice director staff officer.

sentences.zh: 父端，齊奉朝請。

translations.literal: His father Duan was Qi Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Duan was Qi Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 筠孤貧好學，師事沛國劉瓛，強力專精，深爲瓛所器異。

translations.literal: Jun, orphaned and poor, loved learning; he took Liu Huan of Pei as teacher, strove with force and concentrated with refinement, and was deeply valued and regarded as extraordinary by Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he studied under Pei's Liu Huan, worked hard, and won Huan's deep regard.

sentences.zh: 旣長，博通經術，尤明《三禮》。

translations.literal: When grown he broadly mastered the classics, especially the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he mastered the classics, especially the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 齊建武中，起家奉朝請，遷王府行參軍。

translations.literal: In Qi's Jianwu era he first took office as Regular Attendant and was promoted Staff Officer in a princely kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi Jianwu he began as Regular Attendant, then princely staff officer.

sentences.zh: 天監初，爲本州治中，除暨陽令，有清績。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was made Chief Clerk of his native province, then removed as Magistrate of Jiyang with pure achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tianjian he was native-province chief clerk, then Jiyang magistrate with a clean record.

sentences.zh: 入拜尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: He entered court as Gentleman of the Imperial Ancestral Temples in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Secretariat Temples gentleman.

sentences.zh: 七年，安成太妃陳氏薨，江州刺史安成王秀、荊州刺史始興王憺，並以《慈母表》解職，詔不許，還攝本任；

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Honored Consort Chen of Prince of Ancheng died; the Inspector of Jiangzhou, the Prince of Ancheng Xiu, and the Inspector of Jingzhou, the Prince of Shixing Dan, both submitted a Memorial on the Foster Mother to resign office; the edict did not permit it and they resumed their original posts;
translations.idiomatic: In year seven Prince of Ancheng's Honored Consort Chen died; Princes Xiu of Jiangzhou and Dan of Jingzhou petitioned to resign on foster-mother grounds; the throne refused and they kept office;

sentences.zh: 而太妃薨京邑，喪祭無主。

translations.literal: yet the Honored Consort died in the capital and mourning sacrifices had no chief.
translations.idiomatic: but the consort died in the capital with no one to lead the rites.

sentences.zh: 舍人周捨議曰：「賀彥先稱『慈母之子不服慈母之黨，婦又不從夫而服慈姑，小功服無從故也。

translations.literal: Attendant She Zhou She proposed: "He Yanxian said, 'A foster mother's son does not wear mourning for the foster mother's kin; a wife likewise does not follow her husband in wearing mourning for a foster mother-in-law—the lesser mourning has no following, hence.'
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Zhou She argued: "He Yanxian held that a foster mother's son does not mourn her kin, nor a wife her foster mother-in-law—lesser mourning has no following."

sentences.zh: 』庾蔚之云：『非徒子不從母而服其黨，孫又不從父而服其慈母。

translations.literal: Yu Weizhi said: 'It is not only that the son does not follow the mother in wearing mourning for her kin—the grandson likewise does not follow the father in wearing mourning for his foster grandmother.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu Weizhi said the grandson does not follow the father in mourning the foster grandmother."

sentences.zh: 』由斯而言，慈祖母無服明矣。

translations.literal: From this speaking, for a foster grandmother there is clearly no mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Hence no mourning for a foster grandmother is clear."

sentences.zh: 尋門內之哀，不容自同於常；

translations.literal: Seeking grief within the gate, one cannot treat it the same as the ordinary;
translations.idiomatic: Inner-house grief cannot be treated like ordinary mourning;

sentences.zh: 按父之祥禫，子並受弔。

translations.literal: according to the father's auspicious and end-of-mourning rites, sons all receive condolences.
translations.idiomatic: when a father ends mourning, sons all receive condolences.

sentences.zh: 今二王諸子，宜以成服日，單衣一日，爲位受弔。

translations.literal: Now the two princes' sons should on the day of completing mourning wear unlined garments for one day, take position, and receive condolences."
translations.idiomatic: The two princes' sons should on completing mourning wear plain clothes one day and receive condolences."

sentences.zh: 」制曰：「二王在遠，諸子宜攝祭事。

translations.literal: The regulation said: "The two princes are far away; the sons should oversee sacrificial affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The regulation said the distant princes' sons should oversee the sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 」捨又曰：「《禮》云『縞冠玄武，子姓之冠』。

translations.literal: She again said: "The Rites say, 'White cap with dark border—the cap of sons of the lineage.'
translations.idiomatic: She added: "The Rites call the white cap with dark border the cap of lineage sons."

sentences.zh: 則世子衣服宜異於常。

translations.literal: Then the heir's clothing should differ from the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The heir's dress should differ from ordinary dress.

sentences.zh: 可著細布衣，絹爲領帶，三年不聽樂。

translations.literal: He may wear fine cloth garments with silk collar and belt; for three years he does not listen to music.
translations.idiomatic: He may wear fine cloth with silk collar and belt and hear no music for three years.

sentences.zh: 又《禮》及《春秋》：庶母不世祭，蓋謂無王命者耳。

translations.literal: Again the Rites and Spring and Autumn: a concubine mother is not sacrificed to generation after generation—this refers to those without a king's command.
translations.idiomatic: Rites and Spring and Autumn say a concubine mother is not perpetually sacrificed—meaning without royal command.

sentences.zh: 吳太妃旣朝命所加，得用安成禮秩，則當祔廟，五世親盡乃毀。

translations.literal: The Wu Honored Consort, since court command was added, could use Prince of Ancheng's ritual rank—then she should be enshrined in the temple; when kin of five generations is exhausted the shrine is destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Honored Consort, having court rank, should be enshrined and destroyed after five generations.

sentences.zh: 陳太妃命數之重，雖則不異，慈孫旣不從服，廟食理無傳祀，子祭孫止，是會經文。

translations.literal: Chen Honored Consort's weight of command, though not different, since the foster grandson does not follow in mourning, temple offerings by reason have no transmitted sacrifice—son sacrifices, grandson stops: this meets the classic text."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Honored Consort's rank was equal, but the foster grandson does not mourn—no temple sacrifice; son sacrifices, grandson stops: so the classics say."

sentences.zh: 」高祖因是敕禮官議皇子慈母之服。

translations.literal: Gaozu therefore edicted ritual officials to deliberate mourning for a prince's foster mother.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu ordered ritual officials to debate princes' mourning for foster mothers.

sentences.zh: 筠議：「宋朝五服制，皇子服訓養母，依《禮》庶母慈己，宜從小功之制。

translations.literal: Jun proposed: "Song's five-ranks mourning system: a prince wears mourning for a foster mother who reared and taught him; according to the Rites, a concubine mother who was kind to him should follow the lesser mourning regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Jun argued: "Song's system had princes mourn foster mothers; by the Rites a kind concubine mother warrants lesser mourning."

sentences.zh: 按《曾子問》曰：子遊曰：『喪慈母如母，禮歟？

translations.literal: According to the Zengzi Asked: Ziyou said, 'Mourning a foster mother like a mother—is it ritual?'
translations.idiomatic: In Zengzi Asked, Ziyou asked whether mourning a foster mother like a mother was ritual."

sentences.zh: 』孔子曰：『非禮也。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'It is not ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said it was not ritual."

sentences.zh: 古者男子外有傅，內有慈母，君命所使教子也，何服之有？

translations.literal: In antiquity a man outwardly had a tutor, inwardly a foster mother—the ruler's command sent her to teach the son; what mourning is there?'
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity gave a man tutors outside and foster mothers inside by the ruler's command—what mourning is due?"

sentences.zh: 』鄭玄注云：『此指謂國君之子也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan's note says: 'This refers to a feudal lord's son.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan noted this means a feudal lord's son."

sentences.zh: 』若國君之子不服，則王者之子不服可知。

translations.literal: If a feudal lord's son does not wear mourning, then a king's son's not wearing mourning can be known.
translations.idiomatic: If a lord's son does not mourn, a king's son likewise does not."

sentences.zh: 又《喪服經》云『君子子爲庶母慈己者』。

translations.literal: Again the Mourning Dress classic says 'the gentleman's son for a concubine mother who was kind to him.'
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Dress classic says "the gentleman's son for a concubine mother kind to him."

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：『君子子者，貴人子也。

translations.literal: The Tradition says: 'Gentleman's son means a nobleman's son.'
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition says "gentleman's son means a noble's son."

sentences.zh: 』鄭玄引《內則》：三母止施於卿大夫。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan cites the Inner Canon: the three mothers apply only as far as grand masters.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan cites the Inner Canon: the three mothers apply only to grand masters.

sentences.zh: 以此而推，則慈母之服，上不在五等之嗣，下不逮三士之息。

translations.literal: Pushing from this, then mourning for a foster mother above does not reach heirs of the five ranks, below does not reach sons of the three ranks of knights.
translations.idiomatic: Hence foster-mother mourning reaches neither top heirs nor lowest knights.

sentences.zh: 儻其服者止卿大夫，尋諸侯之子尚無此服，況乃施之皇子。

translations.literal: If those who wear it stop at grand masters, tracing further—even a feudal lord's son has no such mourning, how much less applying it to a prince.
translations.idiomatic: If only grand masters mourn, even lords' sons do not—how apply it to princes?

sentences.zh: 謂宜依《禮》刊除，以反前代之惑。

translations.literal: I say it should be cut according to the Rites to return to the confusion of former ages."
translations.idiomatic: It should be struck from the rites to undo former confusion."

sentences.zh: 」高祖以爲不然，曰：「《禮》言慈母，凡有三條：一則妾子之無母，使妾之無子者養之，命爲母子，服以三年，《喪服齊衰章》所言『慈母』是也；

translations.literal: Gaozu thought otherwise and said: "The Rites speak of foster mother in three cases altogether: first, a son of a concubine without a mother—let a concubine without a son rear him, appoint them mother and son, mourning for three years—the 'foster mother' of the Mourning Dress equal mourning chapter is this;
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu disagreed: "The Rites name three foster mothers: first, a concubine's son without a mother reared by a childless concubine—three years' mourning per the equal mourning chapter;"

sentences.zh: 二則嫡妻之子無母，使妾養之，慈撫隆至，雖均乎慈愛，但嫡妻之子，妾無爲母之義，而恩深事重，故服以小功，《喪服小功章》所以不直言慈母，而云『庶母慈己』者，明異於三年之慈母也；

translations.literal: second, a son of the principal wife without a mother—let a concubine rear him; kind care reaches the utmost; though equal in loving kindness, for a son of the principal wife a concubine has no standing as mother, yet favor is deep and the matter weighty—hence lesser mourning; the Mourning Dress lesser mourning chapter therefore does not speak plainly of foster mother but says 'concubine mother kind to him'—making clear the difference from the three-year foster mother;
translations.idiomatic: second, a principal wife's son without a mother reared by a concubine—lesser mourning, called "concubine mother kind to him," not the three-year case;

sentences.zh: 其三則子非無母，正是擇賤者視之，義同師保，而不無慈愛，故亦有慈母之名。

translations.literal: third, the son is not without a mother but precisely one of low rank is chosen to watch him—meaning like tutor and guardian, yet not without loving kindness—hence there is also the name foster mother.
translations.idiomatic: third, a mother exists but a low-ranking nurse is chosen—like tutor and guardian, yet with kindness—also called foster mother.

sentences.zh: 師保旣無其服，則此慈亦無服矣。

translations.literal: Tutor and guardian have no mourning—then this kindness also has no mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Tutors and guardians have no mourning—so this kindness has none either.

sentences.zh: 《內則》云『擇於諸母與可者，使爲子師；

translations.literal: The Inner Canon says 'Choose among the various mothers and the suitable, make her the son's tutor;
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Canon says, "Choose among the mothers and the fit to be the son's tutor;"

sentences.zh: 其次爲慈母；

translations.literal: next make her foster mother;
translations.idiomatic: next foster mother;"

sentences.zh: 其次爲保母』，此其明文。

translations.literal: next make her nurse mother'—this is the plain text.
translations.idiomatic: next nurse mother"—that is the plain text.

sentences.zh: 此言擇諸母，是擇人而爲此三母，非謂擇取兄弟之母也。

translations.literal: This speaking of choosing among mothers is choosing persons to be these three mothers—not choosing a brother's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Choosing among mothers means choosing persons for the three roles—not a brother's mother.

sentences.zh: 何以知之？

translations.literal: How do I know?
translations.idiomatic: How do we know?

sentences.zh: 若是兄弟之母其先有子者，則是長妾，長妾之禮，實有殊加，何容次妾生子，乃退成保母，斯不可也。

translations.literal: If it were a brother's mother who already had a son, she would be the chief concubine; the chief concubine's rites truly have special additions—how could a lesser concubine bear a son and she be demoted to nurse mother? This is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: A brother's mother with a son is chief concubine—how could a lesser concubine's son demote her to nurse? Impossible.

sentences.zh: 又有多兄弟之人，於義或可；

translations.literal: Again, for one with many brothers it might be possible in principle;
translations.idiomatic: For many brothers it might be possible;

sentences.zh: 若始生之子，便應三母俱闕邪？

translations.literal: but for a first-born son, should all three mothers be lacking?
translations.idiomatic: but for a first son, should all three mothers be absent?

sentences.zh: 由是推之，《內則》所言『諸母』，是謂三母，非兄弟之母明矣。

translations.literal: From this pushing, the Inner Canon's 'various mothers' means the three mothers—not brothers' mothers; it is clear."
translations.idiomatic: Hence "various mothers" means the three mothers, not brothers' mothers."

sentences.zh: 子游所問，自是師保之慈，非三年小功之慈也，故夫子得有此對。

translations.literal: What Ziyou asked was precisely tutor-and-guardian kindness, not three-year or lesser mourning kindness—hence the Master could give this answer.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyou asked about tutor-and-guardian kindness, not three-year or lesser mourning—hence the Master's answer.

sentences.zh: 豈非師保之慈母無服之證乎？

translations.literal: Is this not proof that tutor-and-guardian foster mother has no mourning?
translations.idiomatic: Is that not proof tutor-and-guardian foster mothers have no mourning?

sentences.zh: 鄭玄不辨三慈，混爲訓釋，引彼無服，以注『慈己』，後人致謬，實此之由。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan did not distinguish the three kindnesses but mixed them in exegesis, citing the no-mourning case to gloss 'kind to him'—later men's errors truly stem from this.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan confused the three kindnesses and cited no-mourning to gloss "kind to him"—later errors stem from this.

sentences.zh: 經言『君子子』者，此雖起於大夫，明大夫猶爾，自斯以上，彌應不異，故傳云『君子子者，貴人之子也』。

translations.literal: The classic's 'gentleman's son'—though this begins with grand masters, it shows that even grand masters are so; from that upward there should be no difference—hence the Tradition says 'gentleman's son means a nobleman's son.'
translations.idiomatic: Though "gentleman's son" begins with grand masters, if they are included, higher ranks are too—the Tradition says "noble's son."

sentences.zh: 總言曰貴，則無所不包。

translations.literal: Speaking in summary of nobility, nothing is excluded.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of nobility in summary, nothing is excluded.

sentences.zh: 經傳互文，交相顯發，則知慈加之義，通乎大夫以上矣。

translations.literal: Classic and Tradition mutually gloss and illuminate each other—then one knows the meaning of added kindness extends through grand masters and above.
translations.idiomatic: Classic and Tradition together show kindness extends through grand masters and above.

sentences.zh: 宋代此科，不乖《禮》意，便加除削，良是所疑。

translations.literal: Song's category on this does not violate ritual intent; to add cutting and removal is truly doubtful."
translations.idiomatic: Song's rule fits the rites; to cut it is doubtful."

sentences.zh: 」於是筠等請依制改定：嫡妻之子，母沒爲父妾所養，服之五月，貴賤並同，以爲永制。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jun and others asked to fix by regulation: a son of the principal wife, his mother dead and reared by his father's concubine—mourning for five months, noble and common alike the same, as permanent statute."
translations.idiomatic: Jun and others then fixed: a principal wife's son reared by a concubine after his mother's death mourns five months, noble and common alike, as permanent law."

sentences.zh: 累遷王府諮議、權知左丞事，尋除尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession Adviser in a princely kingdom, acting Director of the Left Secretariat, and soon removed as Director of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to princely adviser, acting Left Director, then Left Director.

sentences.zh: 出爲始興內史，卒官。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Shixing and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Shixing and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子壽，傳父業，明《三禮》。

translations.literal: His son Shou inherited his father's profession and was expert in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shou inherited his learning and mastered the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 大同中，歷官尚書祠部郎，出爲曲阿令。

translations.literal: In the Datong era he passed through Gentleman of the Imperial Ancestral Temples in the Secretariat and went out as Magistrate of Qu'e.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong he was Temples gentleman, then Qu'e magistrate.

sentences.zh: 卞華字昭丘，濟陰冤句人也。

translations.literal: Bian Hua, styled Zhaoqiu, was a man of Yuanju in Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Hua, styled Zhaoqiu, was from Yuanju in Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 晉驃騎將軍忠貞公壼六世孫。

translations.literal: Sixth-generation descendant of Jin General of Agile Cavalry and Loyal and Pure Duke Bian.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixth generation from Jin General of Agile Cavalry Loyal and Pure Duke Bian.

sentences.zh: 父倫之，給事中。

translations.literal: His father Lunzhi was Attendant at the Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lunzhi was Palace Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 華幼孤貧好學。

translations.literal: Hua in youth was orphaned and poor yet loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, he loved learning.

sentences.zh: 年十四，召補國子生，通《周易》。

translations.literal: At fourteen he was summoned to fill a place as National University student and mastered the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he entered the National University and mastered the Changes.

sentences.zh: 旣長，遍治《五經》，與平原明山賓、會稽賀瑒同業友善。

translations.literal: When grown he thoroughly studied the Five Classics and with Ming Shanbin of Pingyuan and He Yang of Kuaiji studied together in friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he mastered the Five Classics and studied in friendship with Pingyuan's Ming Shanbin and Kuaiji's He Yang.

sentences.zh: 起家齊豫章王國侍郎，累遷奉朝請、征西行參軍。

translations.literal: He first took office as Gentleman of the Prince of Yuzhang's kingdom in Qi, and was promoted in succession to Court Attendant and staff officer on the Western Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Gentleman of the Qi Prince of Yuzhang's kingdom, then rose to Court Attendant and Western Campaign staff officer.

sentences.zh: 天監初，遷臨川王參軍事，兼國子助教，轉安成王功曹參軍，兼《五經》博士，聚徒教授。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianjian era he was transferred as staff officer to the Prince of Linchuan, concurrently Assistant Instructor at the Imperial University, then became Merit Officer of the Prince of Ancheng and concurrently Doctor of the Five Classics, gathering disciples to teach.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjian he became the Prince of Linchuan's staff officer and Imperial University assistant instructor, then the Prince of Ancheng's merit officer and Five Classics doctor, teaching a large following.

sentences.zh: 華博涉有機辯，說經析理，爲當時之冠。

translations.literal: Hua was broadly learned and quick in debate; in expounding the classics and analyzing principle he was the foremost of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was widely read and sharp in debate; in lecturing and analysis he stood first in his day.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，鐘律絕學，至華乃通焉。

translations.literal: Since the Eastern Jin, pitch-pipes and scales had been a lost study; with Hua it was mastered again.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Eastern Jin, music theory had died out; Hua revived it.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書儀曹郎，出爲吳令，卒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites and sent out as magistrate of Wu, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites, served as magistrate of Wu, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 崔靈恩

translations.literal: Cui Ling'en
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ling'en

sentences.zh: 崔靈恩，清河武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Ling'en was a man of Wucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ling'en was from Wucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 少篤學，從師遍通《五經》，尤精《三禮》、《三傳》。

translations.literal: In youth he was devoted to study; following teachers he mastered the Five Classics throughout, and was especially expert in the Three Rites and the Three Commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied hard, mastered the Five Classics under many teachers, and excelled in the Three Rites and Three Commentaries.

sentences.zh: 先在北仕爲太常博士，天監十三年歸國。

translations.literal: He had first served in the north as Erudite of the Grand Temple; in the thirteenth year of Tianjian he returned to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He had served in the north as Grand Temple erudite and returned home in Tianjian year thirteen.

sentences.zh: 高祖以其儒術，擢拜員外散騎侍郎，累遷步兵校尉，兼國子博士。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor, for his Confucian learning, promoted him to Outer Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and in succession to Commandant of Footsoldiers, concurrently Doctor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu valued his scholarship and made him Outer Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, then Commandant of Footsoldiers and Imperial University doctor.

sentences.zh: 靈恩聚徒講授，聽者常數百人。

translations.literal: Ling'en gathered disciples to lecture; listeners often numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Ling'en taught a large following; audiences often ran to hundreds.

sentences.zh: 性拙朴無風采，及解經析理，甚有精緻，京師舊儒咸稱重之，助教孔僉尤好其學。

translations.literal: By nature he was plain and unadorned, without presence; yet in explaining the classics and analyzing principle he was very refined, and the old scholars of the capital all esteemed him—Assistant Instructor Kong Qian especially favored his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and without airs, he was nonetheless keen in exegesis; capital scholars esteemed him, and Assistant Instructor Kong Qian prized his teaching above all.

sentences.zh: 靈恩先習《左傳》服解，不爲江東所行；

translations.literal: Ling'en had first studied Fu Qian's commentary on the Zuo Tradition, which was not followed east of the Yangzi;
translations.idiomatic: He had first studied Fu Qian on the Zuo Tradition, unused in the southeast;

sentences.zh: 及改說杜義，每文句常申服以難杜，遂著《左氏條義》以明之。

translations.literal: when he turned to expounding Du Yu's meaning, in every phrase he would invoke Fu to challenge Du, and therefore wrote "Entries on the Zuo Tradition" to clarify his view.
translations.idiomatic: then taught Du Yu and constantly used Fu to press Du, writing Entries on the Zuo Tradition to set out his case.

sentences.zh: 時有助教虞僧誕又精杜學，因作《申杜難服》，以報靈恩，世並行焉。

translations.literal: At the time Assistant Instructor Yu Sengdan was also expert in Du's learning and therefore composed "Challenging Fu through Du" in reply to Ling'en; both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Instructor Yu Sengdan, expert in Du, answered with Challenging Fu through Du; both works circulated.

sentences.zh: 僧誕，會稽餘姚人，以《左氏》教授，聽者亦數百人。

translations.literal: Sengdan was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji; he taught the Zuo Tradition, and his listeners too numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Sengdan of Yuyao in Kuaiji taught the Zuo Tradition to hundreds.

sentences.zh: 其該通義例，當時莫及。

translations.literal: His comprehensive mastery of principles and examples was unmatched in the age.
translations.idiomatic: None of the day matched his grasp of principle and example.

sentences.zh: 先是儒者論天，互執渾、蓋二義，論蓋不合於渾，論渾不合於蓋。

translations.literal: Earlier Confucian scholars debating Heaven had each held to the dome or the armillary theories; advocates of the dome did not accord with the armillary, and advocates of the armillary did not accord with the dome.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars had split between dome and armillary theories of Heaven, each side rejecting the other.

sentences.zh: 靈恩立義，以渾、蓋爲一焉。

translations.literal: Ling'en established a doctrine that made dome and armillary one.
translations.idiomatic: Ling'en argued that dome and armillary were one doctrine.

sentences.zh: 出爲長沙內史，還除國子博士，講衆尤盛。

translations.literal: He went out as Interior Governor of Changsha, returned and was appointed Doctor of the Imperial University, and his lecturing audience was especially large.
translations.idiomatic: After governing Changsha he became Imperial University doctor; his audience swelled.

sentences.zh: 出爲明威將軍、桂州刺史，卒官。

translations.literal: He went out as General of Illustrious Might and Inspector of Guizhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as General of Illustrious Might and Inspector of Guizhou and died in office.

sentences.zh: 靈恩集注《毛詩》二十二卷，集注《周禮》四十卷，制《三禮義宗》四十七卷，《左氏經傳義》二十二卷，《左氏條例》十卷，《公羊穀梁文句義》十卷。

translations.literal: Ling'en compiled commentaries on the Mao Odes in twenty-two scrolls, commentaries on the Rites of Zhou in forty scrolls, composed "Summaries of the Meaning of the Three Rites" in forty-seven scrolls, "Meaning of the Zuo Classic and Commentary" in twenty scrolls, "Entries on the Zuo Tradition" in ten scrolls, and "Meaning of the Gongyang and Guliang Textual Phrases" in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His works included twenty-two scrolls on the Mao Odes, forty on the Rites of Zhou, forty-seven on the Three Rites, twenty on the Zuo classic and commentary, ten Zuo entries, and ten on Gongyang and Guliang phrasing.

sentences.zh: 孔僉，會稽山陰人。

translations.literal: Kong Qian was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Qian was from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 少師事何胤，通《五經》，尤明《三禮》、《孝經》、《論語》，講說並數十遍，生徒亦數百人。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under He Yin, mastered the Five Classics, and was especially expert in the Three Rites, the Classic of Filial Piety, and the Analects; he lectured on each several tens of times, and his students too numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under He Yin, mastered the Five Classics, and excelled in the Three Rites, Filial Piety, and Analects, lecturing each dozens of times to hundreds of pupils.

sentences.zh: 歷官國子助教，三爲《五經》博士，遷尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: In office he was Assistant Instructor at the Imperial University, three times Doctor of the Five Classics, and was promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was Imperial University assistant instructor, thrice Five Classics doctor, then Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 出爲海鹽、山陰二縣令。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of the two counties Haiyan and Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Haiyan and Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 僉儒者，不長政術，在縣無績。

translations.literal: Qian was a Confucian and not skilled in administration; in the counties he achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar without administrative talent, he left no mark as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 太清亂，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the disorders of the Taiqing era he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home amid the Taiqing turmoil.

sentences.zh: 子俶玄，頗涉文學，官至太學博士。

translations.literal: His son Chuxuan dabbled in letters and reached the post of Erudite of the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuxuan took to literature and became Erudite of the Grand Academy.

sentences.zh: 僉兄子元素，又善《三禮》，有盛名，早卒。

translations.literal: Qian's elder brother's son Yuansu was also skilled in the Three Rites, enjoyed great fame, and died young.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Yuansu, famed for the Three Rites, also died young.

sentences.zh: 盧廣，范陽涿人，自云晉司空從事中郎諶之後也。

translations.literal: Lu Guang was a man of Zhuo in Fanyang and claimed descent from Chen, Attendant at the Masters' Lodge under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guang of Zhuo in Fanyang claimed descent from Jin Attendant Chen.

sentences.zh: 諶沒死冉閔之亂，晉中原舊族，諶有後焉。

translations.literal: Chen perished in the chaos of Ran Min; of the old clans of the Central Plains in Jin, Chen had descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Chen died in Ran Min's rebellion; among Jin's central plains families his line survived.

sentences.zh: 廣少明經，有儒術。

translations.literal: Guang in youth understood the classics and possessed Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Guang mastered the classics and Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 天監中歸國。

translations.literal: In the Tianjian era he returned to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He returned south in the Tianjian era.

sentences.zh: 初拜員外散騎侍郎，出爲始安太守，坐事免。

translations.literal: He was first appointed Outer Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, went out as Governor of Shian, and was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He first became Outer Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, governed Shian, and was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 頃之，起爲折沖將軍，配千兵北伐，還拜步兵校尉，兼國子博士，遍講《五經》。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled as General Who Breaks the Charge, assigned a thousand troops for the northern campaign, and on return was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers and concurrently Doctor of the Imperial University, lecturing on the Five Classics throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made General Who Breaks the Charge with a thousand men for the northern campaign; returning, he became Commandant of Footsoldiers and Five Classics doctor, lecturing on all five classics.

sentences.zh: 時北來人，儒學者有崔靈恩、孫詳、蔣顯，並聚徒講說，而音辭鄙拙；

translations.literal: At the time among northerners who came south, the Confucian scholars included Cui Ling'en, Sun Xiang, and Jiang Xian; all gathered disciples to lecture, yet their pronunciation and diction were coarse and clumsy;
translations.idiomatic: Northern scholars such as Cui Ling'en, Sun Xiang, and Jiang Xian all taught large followings, but their speech was crude;

sentences.zh: 惟廣言論清雅，不類北人。

translations.literal: only Guang's discourse was refined and clear, not like a northerner.
translations.idiomatic: only Guang spoke elegantly, unlike a northerner.

sentences.zh: 僕射徐勉，兼通經術，深相賞好。

translations.literal: The Vice Director Xu Mian, who was also versed in the classics, deeply appreciated and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xu Mian, himself learned in the classics, prized him highly.

sentences.zh: 尋遷員外散騎常侍，博士如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Outer Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, his doctorate unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He soon rose to Outer Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry while keeping his doctorate.

sentences.zh: 出爲信武桂陽嗣王長史、尋陽太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk to the Heir of Prince Xinyang of Guiyang and Governor of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief clerk to the Guiyang heir and governor of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 又爲武陵王長史，太守如故，卒官。

translations.literal: He then became Chief Clerk to the Prince of Wuling, his governorship unchanged, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief clerk to the Prince of Wuling, kept his prefecture, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 沈峻字士嵩，吳興武康人。

translations.literal: Shen Jun, courtesy name Shisong, was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jun, styled Shisong, was from Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 家世農夫，至峻好學，與舅太史叔明師事宗人沈麟士門下積年。

translations.literal: His family for generations were farmers; Jun came to love learning and, with his maternal uncle Taishi Shuming, studied for many years under their clansman Shen Linshi.
translations.idiomatic: Farmers for generations, Jun turned to study and, with his uncle Taishi Shuming, spent years under Shen Linshi.

sentences.zh: 晝夜自課，時或睡寐，輒以杖自擊，其篤志如此。

translations.literal: Day and night he set himself lessons; when he sometimes fell asleep he would strike himself with a staff—such was his resolute will.
translations.idiomatic: He studied day and night and beat himself with a staff when he dozed—such was his resolve.

sentences.zh: 麟士卒後，乃出都，遍遊講肆，遂博通《五經》，尤長《三禮》。

translations.literal: After Linshi died he went to the capital, traveled every lecture hall, and thus mastered the Five Classics, especially excelling in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After Linshi's death he went to the capital, visited every school, mastered the Five Classics, and excelled in the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 初爲王國中尉，稍遷侍郎，並兼國子助教。

translations.literal: He first served as Commandant of a princely kingdom, was gradually promoted to Gentleman, and in both posts concurrently served as Assistant Instructor at the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a kingdom commandant, rose to gentleman, and held both posts while assisting at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 時吏部郎陸倕與僕射徐勉書薦峻曰：「《五經》博士庾季達須換，計公家必欲詳擇其人。

translations.literal: At the time the Director of the Ministry of Personnel Lu Chan wrote to Vice Director Xu Mian recommending Jun, saying: "The Doctor of the Five Classics Yu Jida must be replaced; I reckon the court will wish to choose the man with care.
translations.idiomatic: Director Lu Chan wrote Xu Mian recommending Jun: "Five Classics doctor Yu Jida must be replaced; the court will choose carefully.

sentences.zh: 凡聖賢可講之書，必以《周官》立義，則《周官》一書，實爲羣經源本。

translations.literal: Of all books the sages and worthies could lecture on, principle must be established through the Offices of Zhou—thus that book is truly the source and root of the cluster of classics.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred books that can be taught must take the Offices of Zhou as their foundation—that book is the root of the classics.

sentences.zh: 此學不傳，多歷年世，北人孫詳、蔣顯亦經聽習，而音革楚、夏，故學徒不至；

translations.literal: This learning has not been transmitted for many years; northerners Sun Xiang and Jiang Xian also once heard and studied it, yet their accents mixed Chu and Xia, so students did not come;
translations.idiomatic: The subject has been lost for generations; Sun Xiang and Jiang Xian studied it, but their accents mixed north and south, and pupils stayed away;

sentences.zh: 惟助教沈峻，特精此書。

translations.literal: only Assistant Instructor Shen Jun is especially expert in this book.
translations.idiomatic: only Assistant Instructor Shen Jun truly masters it.

sentences.zh: 比日時開講肆，羣儒劉岩、沈宏、沈熊之徒，並執經下坐，北面受業，莫不嘆服，人無間言。

translations.literal: Recently he has opened a lecture hall; the Confucians Liu Yan, Shen Hong, Shen Xiong, and the like all hold the classics and sit below, facing north to receive his teaching—none fail to sigh in admiration, and no one voices dissent.
translations.idiomatic: He has lately opened a hall; Liu Yan, Shen Hong, Shen Xiong, and others sit below with their texts, face north, and all admire him without dissent.

sentences.zh: 第謂宜卽用此人，命其專此一學，周而復始。

translations.literal: I would say this man should be employed at once, ordered to devote himself to this one learning, turning and returning without end.
translations.idiomatic: He should be appointed at once to teach this subject alone, again and again.

sentences.zh: 使聖人正典，廢而更興；

translations.literal: Let the sage's correct canon, though abandoned, rise anew;
translations.idiomatic: Let the sage's canon, though fallen, rise again;

sentences.zh: 累世絕業，傳於學者。

translations.literal: let learning cut off for generations pass to scholars.
translations.idiomatic: let a craft lost for generations pass to students.

sentences.zh: 」勉從之，奏峻兼《五經》博士。

translations.literal: " Mian followed this and memorialized Jun as concurrent Doctor of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: " Mian agreed and memorialized Jun as concurrent Five Classics doctor.

sentences.zh: 於館講授，聽者常數百人。

translations.literal: At the academy he lectured; listeners often numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured at the academy to audiences of hundreds.

sentences.zh: 出爲華容令，還除員外散騎侍郎，復兼《五經》博士。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Huarong, returned and was appointed Outer Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and again served concurrently as Doctor of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: After Huarong he became Outer Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and again Five Classics doctor.

sentences.zh: 時中書舍人賀琛奉敕撰《梁官》，乃啓峻及孔子袪補西省學士，助撰錄。

translations.literal: At the time Palace Secretary He Chen received an edict to compile the "Offices of Liang" and therefore memorialized Jun and Kong Ziqu to be added as Western Department academicians to assist in compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretary He Chen, compiling the Offices of Liang, named Jun and Kong Ziqu Western Department academicians to assist.

sentences.zh: 書成，入兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: When the book was finished he entered service concurrently as Palace Secretary for General Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was done he became Palace Secretary for General Affairs.

sentences.zh: 出爲武康令，卒官。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Wukang and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Wukang and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子文阿，傳父業，尤明《左氏傳》。

translations.literal: His son Wen'a inherited his father's craft and was especially expert in the Zuo Tradition.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wen'a followed his father and excelled in the Zuo Tradition.

sentences.zh: 太清中，自國子助教爲《五經》博士。

translations.literal: In the Taiqing era he rose from Assistant Instructor at the Imperial University to Doctor of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiqing he rose from Imperial University assistant to Five Classics doctor.

sentences.zh: 傳峻業者，又有吳郡張及、會稽孔子雲，官皆至《五經》博士、尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: Those who transmitted Jun's craft also included Zhang Ji of Wu commandery and Kong Ziyun of Kuaiji; all reached the posts of Doctor of the Five Classics and Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji of Wu and Kong Ziyun of Kuaiji also carried on his teaching and became Five Classics doctors and Gentlemen of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 太史叔明

translations.literal: Taishi Shuming
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Shuming

sentences.zh: 太史叔明，吳興烏程人，吳太史慈後也。

translations.literal: Taishi Shuming was a man of Wucheng in Wuxing and a descendant of Wu's Taishi Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Shuming of Wucheng in Wuxing was descended from Wu's Taishi Ci.

sentences.zh: 少善《莊》、《老》，兼治《孝經》、《禮記》，其三玄尤精解，當世冠絕，每講說，聽者常五百餘人。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled in the Zhuangzi and Laozi and also studied the Classic of Filial Piety and the Record of Rites; in the Three Mysteries he was especially refined in explanation, unmatched in the age; whenever he lectured, listeners often exceeded five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered Zhuangzi and Laozi, Filial Piety and the Record of Rites, and above all the Three Mysteries; audiences often exceeded five hundred.

sentences.zh: 歷官國子助教。

translations.literal: In office he was Assistant Instructor at the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Imperial University assistant instructor.

sentences.zh: 邵陵王綸好其學，及出爲江州，攜叔明之鎮。

translations.literal: Prince of Shaoling Lun favored his learning; when Lun went out as governor of Jiangzhou he took Shuming to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shaoling Lun prized his learning and took him to Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 王遷郢州，又隨府，所至輒講授，江外人士皆傳其學焉。

translations.literal: When the prince moved to Yingzhou Shuming followed the headquarters; wherever they arrived he lectured, and gentlemen beyond the river all transmitted his learning.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince moved to Yingzhou he followed and lectured everywhere; men south of the Yangzi spread his teaching.

sentences.zh: 大同十三年，卒，時年七十三。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Datong he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Datong year thirteen, aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 孔子袪

translations.literal: Kong Ziqu
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ziqu

sentences.zh: 孔子袪，會稽山陰人。

translations.literal: Kong Ziqu was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Ziqu was from Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧好學，耕耘樵采，常懷書自隨，投閑則誦讀。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he loved learning; while plowing and gathering firewood he always carried books with him and, when free, recited them.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he studied while farming and cutting wood, books always at hand for spare moments.

sentences.zh: 勤苦自勵，遂通經術，尤明《古文尚書》。

translations.literal: Through hard striving he mastered the classics, especially the Ancient Text Book of Documents.
translations.idiomatic: By relentless effort he mastered the classics, especially the Ancient Text Documents.

sentences.zh: 初爲長沙嗣王侍郎，兼國子助教，講《尚書》四十遍，聽者常數百人。

translations.literal: He first served as Gentleman to the Heir of the Prince of Changsha, concurrently Assistant Instructor at the Imperial University; he lectured on the Documents forty times and listeners often numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He began as gentleman to the Changsha heir and Imperial University assistant, lecturing on the Documents forty times to hundreds.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人賀琛受敕撰《梁官》，啓子袪爲西省學士，助撰錄。

translations.literal: Palace Secretary He Chen received an edict to compile the "Offices of Liang" and memorialized Ziqu as Western Department academician to assist in compilation.
translations.idiomatic: He Chen, compiling the Offices of Liang, named Ziqu a Western Department academician.

sentences.zh: 書成，兼司文侍郎，不就。

translations.literal: When the book was finished he was concurrently appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Letters but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished he was offered Vice Director of the Bureau of Letters and declined.

sentences.zh: 久之兼主客郎、舍人，學士如故。

translations.literal: After long service he was concurrently Master of Guests and Secretary, his academician post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Later he doubled as Master of Guests and secretary while remaining an academician.

sentences.zh: 累遷湘東王國侍郎、常侍、員外散騎侍郎，又云麾廬江公記室參軍，轉兼中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Gentleman of the Prince of Xiangdong's kingdom, Regular Attendant, and Outer Attendant of Scattered Cavalry; he also served as Recorder on the staff of the Duke of Lujiang, Cloud-Banner General, and was transferred to concurrent Palace Secretary for General Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts in the Xiangdong princedom to Regular and Outer Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, served the Duke of Lujiang as recorder, and became Palace Secretary for General Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋遷步兵校尉，舍人如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Commandant of Footsoldiers, his secretary post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Commandant of Footsoldiers while keeping his secretary post.

sentences.zh: 高祖撰《五經講疏》及《孔子正言》，專使子袪檢閱羣書，以爲義證。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor composed "Expository Lectures on the Five Classics" and the "Correct Words of Confucius" and specially ordered Ziqu to examine the mass of books as textual proofs.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wrote Expository Lectures on the Five Classics and Correct Words of Confucius and had Ziqu collate the libraries for evidence.

sentences.zh: 事竟，敕子袪與右衛朱异、左丞賀琛於士林館遞日執經。

translations.literal: When the task was done he was ordered, with Right Guard Zhu Yi and Left Director He Chen, to hold the classics in turn at the Scholars' Grove.
translations.idiomatic: When finished he was ordered with Zhu Yi and He Chen to lecture in turn at the Scholars' Grove.

sentences.zh: 累遷通直正員郎，舍人如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Direct Regular Attendant, his secretary post unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Direct Regular Attendant while remaining secretary.

sentences.zh: 中大同元年，卒官，時年五十一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongdatong he died in office, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in Zhongdatong year one, aged fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 子袪凡著《尚書義》二十卷，《集注尚書》三十卷，續朱异《集注周易》一百卷，續何承天《集禮論》一百五十卷。

translations.literal: Ziqu in all composed "Meaning of the Documents" in twenty scrolls, "Collected Commentary on the Documents" in thirty scrolls, continued Zhu Yi's "Collected Commentary on the Changes" in one hundred scrolls, and continued He Chengtian's "Collected Discussions on Rites" in one hundred fifty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His works included twenty scrolls on the Documents, thirty of collected commentary, one hundred continuing Zhu Yi on the Changes, and one hundred fifty continuing He Chengtian on rites.

sentences.zh: 皇侃，吳郡人，青州刺史皇象九世孫也。

translations.literal: Huang Kan was a man of Wu commandery, ninth-generation descendant of Regional Inspector Huang Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Kan of Wu commandery was ninth in descent from Regional Inspector Huang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 侃少好學，師事賀瑒，精力專門，盡通其業，尤明《三禮》、《孝經》、《論語》。

translations.literal: Kan in youth loved learning; he studied under He Yan, devoted his energy to a single specialty, and fully mastered his teacher's craft, especially excelling in the Three Rites, the Classic of Filial Piety, and the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under He Yan, mastered his teacher's craft, and excelled in the Three Rites, Filial Piety, and Analects.

sentences.zh: 起家兼國子助教，于學講說，聽者數百人。

translations.literal: He first took office as concurrent Assistant Instructor at the Imperial University; at the academy he lectured and listeners numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Imperial University assistant instructor and lectured to hundreds at the academy.

sentences.zh: 撰《禮記講疏》五十卷，書成奏上，詔付秘閣。

translations.literal: He composed "Expository Commentary on the Record of Rites" in fifty scrolls; when the book was finished he presented it, and an edict ordered it deposited in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote fifty scrolls of Expository Commentary on the Record of Rites and, when finished, had it placed in the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 頃之，召入壽光殿講《禮記義》，高祖善之，拜員外散騎侍郎，兼助教如故。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to the Hall of Everlasting Light to lecture on the Meaning of the Record of Rites; the High Ancestor approved and appointed him Outer Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, his assistant instructorship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he lectured on the Record of Rites in the Hall of Everlasting Light; Gaozu praised him and made him Outer Attendant of Scattered Cavalry while keeping his instructorship.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，常日限誦《孝經》二十遍，以擬《觀世音經》。

translations.literal: By nature he was utmost in filial piety; each day he set himself to recite the Classic of Filial Piety twenty times, taking it as parallel to the Scripture of Guanshiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial, he recited the Classic of Filial Piety twenty times daily, as others recite the Guanshiyin scripture.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，解職還鄉里。

translations.literal: When his mother died he resigned and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned and went home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 平西邵陵王欽其學，厚禮迎之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shaoling, Pacifier of the West, admired his learning and welcomed him with generous rites.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shaoling Lun, Pacifier of the West, honored his learning and received him with great ceremony.

sentences.zh: 侃旣至，因感心疾，大同十一年，卒於夏首，時年五十八。

translations.literal: Once Kan arrived he was seized by heart illness; in the eleventh year of Datong he died at Xiashou, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he fell ill at heart; he died at Xiashou in Datong year eleven, aged fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 所撰《論語義》十卷，與《禮記義》並見重於世，學者傳焉。

translations.literal: His "Meaning of the Analects" in ten scrolls, together with his "Meaning of the Record of Rites," were both esteemed in the world, and scholars transmitted them.
translations.idiomatic: His ten-scroll Meaning of the Analects and Meaning of the Record of Rites were both prized and widely transmitted.

translations.literal: Commentary section marker in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: Marker denoting the historian's commentary section in the source text.

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：昔叔孫通講論馬上，桓榮精力凶荒；

translations.literal: Yao Cha, Minister of Personnel of Chen, says: In old times Shusun Tong lectured from horseback, and Huan Rong exerted his strength through famine and chaos;
translations.idiomatic: The historian Yao Cha writes: Shusun Tong once lectured on horseback; Huan Rong labored through famine and chaos;

sentences.zh: 旣逢平定，自致光寵；

translations.literal: once peace came they themselves attained glory and favor;
translations.idiomatic: when peace came they won glory and favor;

sentences.zh: 若夫崔、伏、何、嚴互有焉。

translations.literal: as for Cui, Fu, He, and Yan, each in turn had their share.
translations.idiomatic: Cui, Fu, He, and Yan each had their share in turn.

sentences.zh: 曼容、佟之講道于齊季，不爲時改；

translations.literal: Manrong and Tongzhi lectured on the Way in the late Qi but were not changed by the times;
translations.idiomatic: Manrong and Tongzhi taught the Way in late Qi and would not bend to the age;

sentences.zh: 賀瑒、嚴植之之徒，遭梁之崇儒重道，咸至高官，稽古之力，諸子各盡之矣。

translations.literal: He Yan, Yan Zhizhi, and their like met Liang's honoring of Confucianism and reverence for the Way—all reached high office; the power of investigating antiquity, each in his way, they fully displayed.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan, Yan Zhizhi, and others met Liang's esteem for Confucian learning and rose to high office, each displaying the force of classical scholarship.

sentences.zh: 范縝墨絰僥倖，不遂其志，宜哉。

translations.literal: Fan Zhen, in black mourning garb, sought favor by chance and did not fulfill his aim—fitting indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen wore mourning black yet courted favor and failed of his aim—as he deserved.

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker in the source text.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七三年五月版《梁書》爲本校。

translations.literal: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Liang, May 1973.
translations.idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Liang, May 1973.
